title: Any Unitary Gate Can Be Certified Device-Independently In A Quantum Network
authors: Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Shubhayan Sarkar

Device-independent (DI) certification allows the verification of quantum systems based solely on observed statistics, without assumptions about their internal structure. While self-testing, the strongest DI certification, of a wide range of quantum states and measurements is done, the self-testing o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030802] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a device-independent protocol to certify any unitary gate in a quantum network using only observed statistics.
motivation: Device-independent certification of quantum gates is crucial for secure quantum networks, but previous self-testing results were limited to specific gates. A general method for arbitrary unitary gates was missing.
method: The author constructs a Bell-type scenario involving a quantum network with multiple parties and uses the observed correlations to certify the unitary gate via a self-testing argument based on the structure of the network.
result: The protocol can certify any unitary gate up to a global phase, providing the first fully device-independent certification of arbitrary quantum gates.
conclusion: This work significantly advances device-independent quantum information processing by enabling the verification of universal gate sets, which is essential for scalable quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Anomalous Heat Flows And Quantum Otto Engine With (In)definite Causal Order
authors: Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, And Zhong-Xiao Man
abstract:
Author(s): Qing-Feng Xue, Qi Zhang, Xu-Cai Zhuang, Ying-Jie Zhang, Yun-Jie Xia, Enrico Russo, Giulio Chiribella, Rosario Lo Franco, and Zhong-Xiao Man

The principle that heat spontaneously flows from higher temperatures to lower temperatures is a cornerstone of classical thermodynamics. While this principle holds true for macroscopic systems at equilibrium, here we show that, when a quantum system undergoes two thermalization processes in an indef…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030404] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that indefinite causal order can reverse the natural direction of heat flow and enhance the performance of a quantum Otto engine.
motivation: Classical thermodynamics dictates heat flows from hot to cold; the authors explore whether indefinite causal order in quantum processes can violate this principle and improve engine efficiency.
method: They consider a quantum Otto engine where the two thermalization strokes are arranged in an indefinite causal order using a quantum switch, and analyze the resulting heat flows and work output.
result: Indefinite causal order can cause heat to flow from cold to hot, and the engine can achieve higher efficiency and power than any definite-order engine.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a new resource for quantum thermodynamics, enabling anomalous heat flows and enhanced engine performance beyond classical limits.

title: Planckian Bound On Quantum Dynamical Entropy
authors: Xiangyu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Cao

We introduce a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring’s quantum dynamical entropy for quantum systems. It quantifies the amount of information gained about the initial condition from continuously monitoring an observable. A nonzero entropy growth rate can be obtained by monitoring the therm…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030402] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simplified quantum dynamical entropy that grows linearly in time, with a rate bounded by temperature, linking chaos and thermodynamics.
motivation: To quantify information gain from continuous monitoring in quantum systems and connect entropy growth to physical bounds.
method: Defines a simplified version of Connes-Narnhofer-Thirring entropy for quantum systems, analyzing its growth under continuous measurement of an observable.
result: The entropy growth rate is bounded by a Planckian bound proportional to temperature, providing a quantum analog of classical dynamical entropy.
conclusion: The bound suggests a fundamental limit on information extraction from quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum chaos and thermodynamics.

title: Finite-time Thermal Refrigerator In Interacting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, And Pablo D. Mininni
abstract:
Author(s): Joaquín I. Ganly, Julián Amette Estrada, Franco Mayo, Augusto J. Roncaglia, and Pablo D. Mininni

We study a finite-time thermodynamic refrigeration cycle realized numerically in three-dimensional, weakly interacting Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs). The setup consists of three spatially separated condensates (system, piston, and reservoir) coupled through time-dependent potential barriers that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013315] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A finite-time refrigeration cycle using three interacting Bose-Einstein condensates is numerically demonstrated, achieving cooling below the bath temperature.
motivation: To explore quantum thermodynamic cycles in interacting many-body systems and understand the role of interactions in finite-time refrigeration.
method: Numerical simulations of three coupled BECs with time-dependent potential barriers, implementing a thermodynamic cycle analogous to a quantum refrigerator.
result: The system acts as a refrigerator, cooling the target BEC below the reservoir temperature, with performance depending on interaction strength and cycle duration.
conclusion: Interacting BECs can serve as a platform for finite-time quantum refrigeration, with interactions playing a key role in performance.

title: Trajectory-independent Speed Limits For Controlled Open Quantum Systems
authors: James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, And Christian Arenz
abstract:
Author(s): James B. Larsen, Tameem Albash, Alicia B. Magann, and Christian Arenz

Existing quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems depend on the specified trajectory. For example, lower bounds on quantum annealing times in the presence of dissipation depend explicitly on the chosen annealing schedule. Recently, schedule-independent speed limits have been derived …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012439] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives trajectory-independent quantum speed limits for controlled open quantum systems, providing fundamental bounds on evolution time that depend only on initial and final states.
motivation: Existing quantum speed limits for open systems depend on the control trajectory, making them less fundamental. This work aims to find bounds that are independent of the path taken.
method: Uses geometric and information-theoretic arguments, possibly involving the Bures angle or quantum Fisher information, to derive speed limits that are functions only of the initial and final states and the system's dissipative properties.
result: Obtains trajectory-independent lower bounds on the time required for state transformation under controlled open quantum dynamics, generalizing previous results for closed systems.
conclusion: These bounds provide fundamental thermodynamic constraints on quantum control, relevant for quantum annealing and other controlled processes in dissipative environments.

title: Analytical Construction Of $(n,$ $n−1)$-quantum Random Access Codes Saturating The Conjectured Bound
authors: Takayuki Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Suzuki

Quantum Random Access Codes (QRACs) embody the fundamental trade-off between the compressibility of information into limited quantum resources and the accessibility of that information, serving as a cornerstone of quantum communication and computation. In particular, the [MATH]-QRACs, which encod…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012441] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically constructs (n, n-1)-quantum random access codes that saturate the conjectured bound, providing optimal trade-offs between encoding dimension and decoding success.
motivation: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) are fundamental for understanding the trade-off between information compression and accessibility in quantum communication. The (n, n-1)-QRACs are particularly important, but their optimal performance was only conjectured.
method: The author uses analytical constructions based on mutually unbiased bases and symmetric informationally complete measurements to achieve the optimal success probability for (n, n-1)-QRACs.
result: The constructed QRACs saturate the conjectured bound, proving its tightness for all n. The success probability matches the optimal value derived from semidefinite programming.
conclusion: This work provides a complete analytical solution for (n, n-1)-QRACs, confirming the conjectured bound and offering insights into the structure of optimal quantum encoding schemes.

title: Hybrid Single-ion Atomic-ensemble Node For High-rate Remote Entanglement Generation
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

The authors propose to generate entanglement between trapped ions and broadband photons compatible with ensemble-based memories using spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon sources. Overcoming the bandwidth mismatch between these systems can provide a hybrid quantum network architecture that combines ensemble-based multiplexed entanglement generation and deterministic ion gates, resulting in a significant speed-up in establishing remote ion-ion entanglement over hundreds of kilometers.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum network node combining trapped ions and atomic ensembles for high-rate remote entanglement generation over hundreds of kilometers.
motivation: Current quantum networks suffer from low entanglement generation rates due to bandwidth mismatch between deterministic ion gates and ensemble-based memories; a hybrid architecture can overcome this.
method: The authors design a node using trapped ions for deterministic gates and atomic ensembles for multiplexed entanglement generation, interfaced via broadband SPDC photons, and analyze the rate of remote ion-ion entanglement.
result: The hybrid scheme achieves a significant speed-up in establishing remote entanglement compared to purely ion-based or ensemble-based approaches, with rates suitable for long-distance quantum networks.
conclusion: This hybrid node architecture offers a practical path to scalable quantum networks by combining the strengths of different quantum platforms.

title: Accelerated Relaxation And Mpemba-like Effect For Operators In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect occurs when a quantum system, residing far away from the steady state, relaxes faster than a relatively nearer state. We look for the presence of this highly counterintuitive effect in the relaxation dynamics of the operators within the open quantum system setting. Since th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L010601] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect in the relaxation dynamics of operators in open quantum systems, showing that states farther from steady state can relax faster.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive phenomenon where a system farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one closer. Understanding this effect in open quantum systems can provide insights into non-equilibrium thermodynamics and relaxation processes.
method: The authors study the relaxation of operators in open quantum systems using a Lindblad master equation approach, analyzing the time evolution of operator expectation values and comparing relaxation rates for different initial states.
result: They demonstrate the existence of the Mpemba-like effect for operators, where certain initial operator states exhibit accelerated relaxation compared to others that are initially closer to the steady state.
conclusion: The findings extend the quantum Mpemba effect to operator dynamics, offering a new perspective on relaxation in open quantum systems and potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Photon-mediated Entanglement Between Spin Qubits Beyond The Dispersive Regime
authors: Andrei I. Nikitchenko And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei I. Nikitchenko and Guido Burkard

Dispersively coupled distant qubits in a shared cavity can become entangled through virtual photon exchange with energy-conserving phase evolution of their quantum states. This interaction can potentially be accelerated by operating on resonance, allowing for the exchange of real photons. In this th…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045420] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates photon-mediated entanglement between spin qubits beyond the dispersive regime, enabling faster entanglement generation via real photon exchange.
motivation: Dispersive coupling is slow; operating on resonance could accelerate entanglement but introduces decoherence. The authors aim to show that resonant coupling can still produce high-fidelity entanglement.
method: They theoretically analyze two spin qubits coupled to a common cavity, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and solving the dynamics for both dispersive and resonant regimes, including the effects of photon loss.
result: They find that resonant operation can generate entanglement faster than the dispersive regime while maintaining comparable fidelity under realistic cavity decay rates.
conclusion: Resonant photon-mediated coupling is a viable route to faster two-qubit gates in spin qubit systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and distributed quantum computing.

title: Fluctuation-response Relation For A Nonequilibrium System With Resolved Markovian Embedding
authors: Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Rémi Goerlich, Antoine Tartar, Yael Roichman, and Igor M. Sokolov

Fluctuation-response relations must be modified to describe nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that such relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved. Using a colloidal partic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014138] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that fluctuation-response relations for non-Markovian nonequilibrium systems can be recovered by explicitly resolving the Markovian embedding of the dynamics.
motivation: Fluctuation-response relations are fundamental in equilibrium systems but require modification for nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics. The authors aim to quantitatively recover such relations by resolving the hidden Markovian degrees of freedom.
method: Using a colloidal particle in a time-dependent optical trap, the authors experimentally realize a non-Markovian system and reconstruct the Markovian embedding by measuring the full dynamics of the particle and its environment.
result: They show that the fluctuation-response relation holds when the Markovian embedding is explicitly accounted for, providing a direct experimental verification of the theoretical framework.
conclusion: The work validates that non-Markovian fluctuation-response relations can be understood through Markovian embedding, offering a practical approach to characterize nonequilibrium systems with memory.

title: Restoring Detailed Balance In non-Hermitian Markov Processes
authors: Tim van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, And Christophe Deroulers
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Van Wesemael, Gilberto Nakamura, Jan Baetens, Odemir M. Bruno, Alexandre S. Martinez, and Christophe Deroulers

Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often involve asymmetric contributions that break detailed balance and lead to nonmonotonic entropy production, limiting thermodynamic interpretations and inference techniques. Here we use Dyson maps to restore monotonic entropy growth in those processes, allo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014131] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Dyson maps to restore detailed balance in non-Hermitian Markov processes, enabling monotonic entropy production and thermodynamic interpretation.
motivation: Stochastic out-of-equilibrium processes often break detailed balance, leading to nonmonotonic entropy production that limits thermodynamic analysis and inference.
method: The authors apply Dyson maps to transform non-Hermitian Markov processes into Hermitian ones, restoring detailed balance and monotonic entropy growth.
result: The method yields monotonic entropy production and allows thermodynamic interpretation of previously intractable non-equilibrium processes.
conclusion: Dyson maps provide a systematic way to restore detailed balance, broadening the scope of thermodynamic analysis for non-Hermitian stochastic systems.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems undergoing sudden quenches, showing that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three candidate definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for quench processes, and test them against the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All three definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of them are consistent with the second law.
conclusion: The study provides guidance on which definitions of thermodynamic quantities are physically meaningful for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unified Speed Limits In Classical And Quantum Dynamics Via Temporal Fisher Information
authors: Tomohiro Nishiyama And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tomohiro Nishiyama and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

The importance of Fisher information is increasing in nonequilibrium thermodynamics, as it has played a fundamental role in trade-off relations such as thermodynamic uncertainty relations and speed limits. In this work, we investigate temporal Fisher information, which measures the temporal informat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014120] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies classical and quantum speed limits using temporal Fisher information, establishing a fundamental trade-off between the rate of change of a system and the Fisher information about time.
motivation: Speed limits are crucial in thermodynamics and quantum information, but a unified framework for classical and quantum systems was lacking. The authors aim to derive a general bound using Fisher information.
method: The authors define temporal Fisher information for both classical and quantum dynamics and prove that the speed of state change is bounded by the square root of the Fisher information. They apply this to various examples including unitary evolution and open quantum systems.
result: They obtain a unified speed limit that recovers known classical and quantum bounds, and show that the Fisher information provides a tighter bound than previous approaches in certain regimes.
conclusion: Temporal Fisher information offers a powerful tool to unify speed limits across classical and quantum dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Enhanced Tripartite Interaction In A magnon-Andreev-superconducting Qubit Hybrid System: Collapse-revival Phenomena And Entanglement Redistribution
authors: Sheng Zhao And Peng-Bo Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhao and Peng-Bo Li

Tripartite interactions are fundamental for realizing quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics, yet their native implementation—particularly among distinct quantum systems—remains challenging. Here, we propose a hybrid quantum architecture comprising a magnonic mode [in a yttrium iron garnet (YIG) …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033074] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid magnon-Andreev-superconducting qubit system that realizes enhanced tripartite interactions, leading to collapse-revival phenomena and entanglement redistribution.
motivation: Native tripartite interactions among distinct quantum systems are challenging but essential for quantum phenomena beyond pairwise physics.
method: The system couples a magnonic mode in YIG, an Andreev qubit, and a superconducting qubit via a common transmission line resonator, enabling controllable tripartite coupling.
result: Enhanced tripartite interaction strength is achieved, leading to collapse-revival dynamics in the magnon population and redistribution of entanglement among the three subsystems.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid platform provides a viable route to realize and control tripartite quantum effects, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Detecting Strongly non-Gaussian Entanglement
authors: Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, And Nicolas J. Cerf
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Deside, Tobias Haas, and Nicolas J. Cerf

Efficiently certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable quantum systems is a central challenge for advancing quantum information processing, photonic quantum computing, and metrology. Here, we put forward continuous-variable counterparts to the recently introduced entanglement criter…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes continuous-variable entanglement criteria based on higher-order moments to detect strongly non-Gaussian entanglement.
motivation: Certifying non-Gaussian entanglement in continuous-variable systems is crucial for quantum information processing but remains challenging due to the limitations of Gaussian criteria.
method: Derives entanglement witnesses using higher-order moments (e.g., fourth-order) and applies them to non-Gaussian states such as photon-subtracted squeezed states and cat states.
result: The criteria can detect entanglement in states where Gaussian criteria fail, and are experimentally feasible with homodyne detection.
conclusion: The proposed criteria provide a practical tool for certifying non-Gaussian entanglement, advancing continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Single- And Double-click High-rate Entanglement Generation Between Distant Ions Using Multiplexed Atomic Ensembles
authors: Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Benedikt Tissot, Soubhadra Maiti, Emil R. Hellebek, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

In an accompanying paper [B. Tissot et al.,
tldr: Proposes a high-rate entanglement generation scheme between distant trapped ions using multiplexed atomic ensembles and SPDC sources.
motivation: To enable fast and efficient entanglement distribution between remote quantum processors, which is essential for scalable quantum networks.
method: Combines trapped-ion quantum processors with ensemble-based quantum memories via a spontaneous parametric down-conversion source, using multiplexing to enhance entanglement generation rates.
result: Achieves high entanglement generation rates with both single-click and double-click protocols, significantly outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: The proposed interface offers a practical path toward high-rate entanglement distribution for quantum networks, leveraging existing technologies.

title: Partially Device-independent Quantum Cryptography In Asymmetric Networks
authors: Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, And Kai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Hao Wei, Shu-Ming Hu, Nuo-Ya Yang, Shuai Zhao, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, and Kai Chen

Quantum key distribution (QKD) enables secure key generation between distant users, yet its standard device-dependent implementations rely on fully characterized and accurately modeled devices. Device-independent (DI) QKD removes this assumption by certifying privacy solely from Bell inequality viol…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033060] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a partially device-independent QKD protocol for asymmetric networks, using one trusted and one untrusted node to achieve high key rates with minimal trust assumptions.
motivation: Standard device-independent QKD requires both parties to be untrusted, which is inefficient for asymmetric networks where one node may be trusted. The authors aim to bridge the gap between device-dependent and fully device-independent QKD.
method: The protocol combines a trusted measurement device on one side with an untrusted Bell-test on the other, using entropy accumulation and security proofs based on the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The protocol achieves key rates comparable to device-dependent QKD while providing security against untrusted devices on the untrusted side, demonstrated through finite-size analysis and simulation.
conclusion: Partially device-independent QKD offers a practical trade-off between security and performance for asymmetric quantum networks, making it suitable for real-world deployment.

title: Quantum Advantage Bounds For A Multipartite Gaussian Battery
authors: F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, And M. Sassetti
abstract:
Author(s): F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, M. Carrega, G. Benenti, and M. Sassetti

We demonstrate the possibility of a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of quantum batteries by analyzing a model that enables a consistent comparison between quantum and classical regimes. Our system consists of [MATH] harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common thermal reservoir, evolving t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033045] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a genuine quantum advantage in the efficiency of a multipartite Gaussian battery, modeled as harmonic oscillators coupled to a common thermal reservoir.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but a fair comparison between quantum and classical regimes is needed to confirm genuine quantum advantage.
method: The authors analyze a model of harmonic oscillator cells coupled to a common reservoir, evolving under a charging protocol, and compare the charging power and efficiency in quantum versus classical regimes.
result: They find that quantum correlations among the cells lead to a higher charging efficiency, establishing a quantum advantage that is bounded by the amount of entanglement.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous bounds on quantum advantage in battery charging, highlighting the role of entanglement and offering design principles for quantum-enhanced energy storage.

title: Operational Coherent Measurements With Steering And Randomness
authors: Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, And Hsi-Sheng Goan
abstract:
Author(s): Chellasamy Jebarathinam, Huan-Yu Ku, and Hsi-Sheng Goan

Measurement incompatibility underpins randomness generation in nonlocal phenomena. However, at its root, a more fundamental quantum feature is noncommuting (or coherent) measurements. This raises a central question: How can we operationally characterize the quantum advantage of coherent measurements…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033054] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper operationally characterizes the quantum advantage of coherent measurements through steering and randomness generation.
motivation: Measurement incompatibility is known to underpin randomness generation, but the fundamental role of coherent (noncommuting) measurements is not fully understood operationally.
method: The authors develop a framework linking coherent measurements to steering and randomness, using quantum information-theoretic tools to quantify the advantage.
result: They show that coherent measurements provide a quantum advantage in steering and randomness generation beyond what is possible with incompatible but non-coherent measurements.
conclusion: Coherent measurements are a key resource for operational tasks like randomness generation, and their advantage can be characterized via steering.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved using noisy quantum networks that distribute noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information.
motivation: Distributed sensing with quantum networks promises enhanced precision, but practical networks are noisy. The authors aim to show that even with noisy entanglement distribution, quantum advantage over classical strategies is possible.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states subject to noise, and compare the QFI to the optimal classical Fisher information.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for a range of noise levels and network sizes, and provide explicit conditions under which the noisy quantum network outperforms classical sensing.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still provide a quantum advantage in distributed sensing, which is encouraging for practical implementations of quantum-enhanced sensor networks.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots
authors: Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, And Gianluca Rastelli
abstract:
Author(s): Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, and Gianluca Rastelli

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates single microwave photon detection using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity within circuit QED.
motivation: Detecting single microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but remains challenging due to low energies and noise.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot tunnel-coupled to a lead interacts dispersively with a microwave cavity, and analyze the photon-induced current through the dot.
result: They show that a single photon can induce a measurable current change under optimized parameters, enabling high-fidelity detection.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable path toward single microwave photon detection using quantum dots, with potential applications in quantum networks and sensing.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws for charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging via collective effects, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in open systems is not fully understood.
method: The authors study N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum batteries under Gaussian driving and dissipation, using Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models to derive scaling laws for charging power and entanglement.
result: They find that superabsorption leads to power scaling as O(N^2) in the ideal case, with entanglement playing a key role, and identify dynamical scaling laws that persist under realistic open-system conditions.
conclusion: Collective quantum effects can significantly enhance battery performance, and the scaling laws provide design principles for experimental quantum batteries.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active stabilization; existing methods are complex and resource-intensive.
method: Employs a cascaded quantum network architecture with a squeezed reservoir to autonomously stabilize entanglement between two remote qubits.
result: Achieves stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, robust against realistic imperfections and noise.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable and practical approach for maintaining entanglement in quantum networks.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.
method: Two spatially separated superconducting qubits are coupled to a common squeezed microwave reservoir, which generates and distributes entanglement autonomously.
result: Stationary qubit entanglement is achieved and characterized, showing high fidelity and rate suitable for networking applications.
conclusion: Nonlocal squeezed reservoirs offer a promising platform for scalable entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting the nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedups.
motivation: To clarify and categorize the various forms of quantum advantage that have been discovered, beyond the well-known exponential speedup for factoring.
method: The authors survey and classify different types of quantum advantage, including computational, communication, sensing, and thermodynamic advantages, using examples from recent literature.
result: They identify a rich spectrum of quantum advantages, ranging from exponential to polynomial speedups, as well as advantages in communication complexity, metrology, and thermodynamics.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is a multifaceted concept; understanding its full scope is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, introducing a criterion that separates classical and nonclassical processes.
result: The unified rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness and identifies intrinsically quantum properties in many phenomena long considered classical.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is fragile and typically requires precise control; the authors aim to harness dissipation as a resource to create and stabilize multipartite entangled states in a scalable and reconfigurable manner.
method: They couple multiple spin ensembles to a common cavity and engineer dissipative dynamics via cavity loss, using a combination of drive fields and cavity-mediated interactions to stabilize desired entangled states.
result: They show that the dissipative protocol can generate a variety of entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states, with high fidelity and robustness against imperfections.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to scalable entanglement generation for quantum sensing and many-body physics, leveraging dissipation as a tool rather than an obstacle.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive schemes could offer simpler, faster protection.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction protocol using continuous drives in a superconducting cavity to protect against photon loss, without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the system, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to improve performance.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform physical limits, suggesting a new path for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies and mitigates loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence time and cooperativity.
motivation: Mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits are promising for quantum information processing, but their performance is limited by loss mechanisms that are not fully understood.
method: The authors optimize the piezoelectric transducer's properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize loss channels through systematic experiments and materials analysis.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and provide a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding and performance of hybrid quantum systems involving mechanical resonators and superconducting circuits, enabling better quantum transducers and memory.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity.
motivation: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation requires high-fidelity logical Bell pairs, but existing methods have high overhead or require complex connectivity.
method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to distill a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly lower spacetime volume compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: This work enables practical distributed quantum computation by reducing the resource overhead for logical Bell pair generation.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector as an autonomous machine and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using entropy production and measurement accuracy metrics.
result: They demonstrate a fundamental trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires greater thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of the thermodynamic limits of information acquisition in quantum systems, with implications for quantum metrology and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global microwave pulses and optical heralding to generate and stabilize large cluster states.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with low overhead, scalable to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking and computation.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can improve the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding monitored quantum dynamics and the role of measurements in error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the decodability of quantum codes under random monitoring, using statistical mechanics mappings and logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and identify conditions for stability under partial measurement.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, offering new insights into the interplay between measurements and code performance.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and sensitivity to losses. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical codes.
method: They introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs significantly reduce the required number of emitters and improve the loss tolerance of quantum repeaters, making them more feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level spin defect in ZnO with exceptional coherence and readout fidelity, positioning ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Current quantum platforms face challenges in scalability and coherence; wide-bandgap oxides like ZnO may offer new defect-based qubits with superior properties.
method: The authors characterize the spin defect using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements, demonstrating long coherence time and high-fidelity single-shot readout.
result: The defect exhibits a 4-ms spin coherence time, unusually small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity, enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections; a framework is needed to rigorously account for device characterization in security proofs.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization into composable security proofs, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
result: The method yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of QKD devices, enabling practical security guarantees.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, advancing the certification of QKD systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme yields a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression via erasure conversion, enhancing prospects for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Experimental Evidence For Strong Emergent Correlations Between Particles In A Switching Trap
authors: Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, And Grégory Schehr
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Biroli, Sergio Ciliberto, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar, Artyom Petrosyan, and Grégory Schehr

We experimentally study a system of [MATH] two-dimensional Brownian particles, each confined in a harmonic trap with identical stiffness. The stiffness switches simultaneously between two values at random Poissonian times. This collective switching drives the system into a nonequilibrium stationary s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of Brownian particles in a switching trap reveals strong emergent correlations in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how collective switching drives correlations in many-particle systems out of equilibrium.
method: Experiment with 2D Brownian particles in harmonic traps whose stiffness switches randomly between two values, measuring particle positions and correlations.
result: Strong emergent correlations between particles are observed in the nonequilibrium stationary state.
conclusion: Collective switching can induce significant correlations, relevant for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics and information thermodynamics.

title: Inverse Clausius Thermodynamics In Run-and-Tumble Dynamics
authors: Oded Farago
abstract:
Author(s): Oded Farago

We establish a mapping between one-dimensional run-and-tumble particle dynamics in the presence of thermal noise, and overdamped Brownian motion in a spatially inhomogeneous temperature field. The approach is formulated as an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework, where the effective temperature …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 037103] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a mapping between run-and-tumble particle dynamics and Brownian motion in inhomogeneous temperature, formulating an inverse-Clausius thermodynamic framework.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamics of active matter systems, specifically run-and-tumble particles, which are out of equilibrium and exhibit complex dynamics.
method: Derives an effective temperature field that maps the run-and-tumble dynamics to overdamped Brownian motion, using an inverse-Clausius approach.
result: The mapping reveals that the active system can be described by an effective temperature that depends on the particle's position, linking activity to thermodynamic concepts.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic perspective on active matter, showing that run-and-tumble dynamics can be understood through an effective temperature field, which may have implications for understanding non-equilibrium systems.

title: General Concurrence Percolation On Quantum Networks
authors: Deep Nath And Soumen Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Deep Nath and Soumen Roy

A quantum network is a network of entangled states which can be used to transmit quantum information. Nonmaximally entangled states are not really effective in establishing quantum communication across vast distances. Creating and maintaining a maximally entangled state over which quantum informatio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012440] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general concurrence percolation framework for quantum networks, analyzing entanglement distribution and percolation thresholds for non-maximally entangled states.
motivation: Non-maximally entangled states are less effective for long-distance quantum communication, so understanding percolation of concurrence in quantum networks is crucial for designing robust entanglement distribution protocols.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for concurrence percolation on quantum networks, considering both classical and quantum percolation regimes, and derive conditions for successful entanglement distribution.
result: They find that concurrence percolation exhibits a threshold behavior dependent on network topology and initial entanglement, and that quantum strategies can outperform classical ones in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for designing efficient quantum network architectures using non-maximally entangled states, with implications for quantum repeaters and multi-party communication.

title: Long-term Stability Of Quantum Resources Through Gravitational Cat States In A Dissipative Markovian Environment
authors: Anas Ait Chlih And Tamer A. Seoudy
abstract:
Author(s): Anas Ait Chlih and Tamer A. Seoudy

The paradigm in which gravity can generate entanglement between distant masses represents a profound shift in our understanding of quantum-gravitational interfaces and is still among the active and debated topics. Recent work [A. ur Rahman et al.,
tldr: This paper investigates the long-term stability of quantum resources (entanglement, discord, coherence) in gravitational cat states under a dissipative Markovian environment.
motivation: Understanding how gravity affects quantum resources is crucial for quantum-gravitational interfaces, but the stability of these resources in realistic noisy environments is unknown.
method: The authors model a gravitational cat state interacting with a dissipative Markovian environment and analyze the dynamics of entanglement, discord, and coherence using standard measures.
result: They find that certain quantum resources can be preserved for long times under specific conditions, with entanglement and discord showing different decay behaviors.
conclusion: Gravitational cat states can serve as robust quantum resources in noisy environments, with potential applications in quantum information processing and tests of quantum gravity.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of The Lindblad Master Equation And Its Nonlinear Extensions Via Quantum Trajectory Averaging
authors: Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, And Shu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Guo Liu, Heng Fan, and Shu Chen

Since precisely controlling dissipation in realistic environments is challenging, digital simulation of the Lindblad master equation (LME) is of great significance for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems. However, achieving long-time simulations for complex systems with mul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012436] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a digital quantum simulation method for the Lindblad master equation and its nonlinear extensions using quantum trajectory averaging.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems is crucial for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics, but long-time simulations are challenging; digital simulation offers a scalable approach.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that averages over quantum trajectories to simulate both linear and nonlinear Lindblad master equations on digital quantum computers.
result: The method achieves accurate simulation of dissipative dynamics and nonlinear extensions, with complexity scaling favorably with system size and simulation time.
conclusion: This work provides a practical digital quantum simulation framework for open quantum systems, enabling study of non-equilibrium thermodynamics and quantum thermal machines.

title: Precision-induced Irreversibility In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, And Diego Bautista Avilés
abstract:
Author(s): Luis E. F. Foa Torres, Giorgos Pappas, Vassos Achilleos, and Diego Bautista Avilés

Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, yet finite dynamic range imposes a sharp operational limit on reversibility. We identify precision-induced irreversibility: Amplification, mode mixing (as warranted by non-normality), and a finite resolution floor—whether set by detector noise, e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012207] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies precision-induced irreversibility in non-Hermitian systems due to finite dynamic range, linking amplification and mode mixing to operational limits on reversibility.
motivation: Non-Hermitian evolution is mathematically invertible, but practical reversibility is limited by finite resolution. The authors aim to characterize this irreversibility from an information-thermodynamic perspective.
method: The authors analyze non-Hermitian systems with amplification and non-normality, incorporating a finite resolution floor (e.g., detector noise) to model operational limits. They derive bounds on reversibility based on precision.
result: They show that amplification and mode mixing, combined with finite resolution, lead to an irreversible loss of information, quantified by a precision-dependent entropy increase.
conclusion: Precision-induced irreversibility is a fundamental constraint in non-Hermitian systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing in open systems.

title: Detection Of Mpemba Effect Through Observables In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, And Bijay Kumar Agarwalla
abstract:
Author(s): Pitambar Bagui, Arijit Chatterjee, and Bijay Kumar Agarwalla

The quantum Mpemba effect refers to the anomalous relaxation of a quantum state that, despite being initially farther from the steady state, relaxes faster than a closer counterpart. Detecting such a quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state during its time evoluti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014311] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to detect the quantum Mpemba effect using only observable quantities, without full state tomography.
motivation: Detecting the quantum Mpemba effect typically requires full knowledge of the quantum state, which is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to provide a simpler detection method based on observables.
method: The authors derive conditions for the Mpemba effect in open quantum systems using the time evolution of expectation values of observables, and illustrate with examples of qubit and harmonic oscillator systems.
result: They show that the Mpemba effect can be detected by monitoring a single observable, such as energy or magnetization, and provide criteria based on the observable's relaxation rate.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for identifying the quantum Mpemba effect in experiments, advancing the understanding of anomalous relaxation in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Growth And Spreading Of Quantum Resources Under Random Circuit Dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, And Piotr Sierant
abstract:
Author(s): Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, and Piotr Sierant

Quantum many-body dynamics generate nonclassical correlations naturally described by quantum resource theories. Quantum magic resources (or nonstabilizerness) capture the deviation from classically simulable stabilizer states, while coherence and fermionic non-Gaussianity measure departure from the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033062] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the growth and spreading of quantum magic resources under random unitary circuit dynamics, providing analytical and numerical results for the generation of nonstabilizerness.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic (nonstabilizerness) spread in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing computational complexity and the onset of quantum advantage.
method: The authors use random unitary circuits as a minimal model for quantum dynamics and compute the average and variance of magic measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) using tools from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
result: They find that magic grows linearly in time and saturates to a volume-law value, with the saturation value depending on the local Hilbert space dimension and the circuit architecture.
conclusion: The results establish a universal framework for the dynamical generation of magic in chaotic quantum systems, linking resource theory to many-body dynamics.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, compact and efficient interfaces between stationary qubits (neutral atoms) and flying qubits (photons) are needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fibers on a chip, and characterize its performance for photon collection and coupling.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon extraction and stable, compact operation suitable for quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical building block for future quantum network nodes, advancing experimental quantum networking.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg lifetimes due to blackbody radiation. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, measuring Rydberg lifetimes at various temperatures and comparing to theoretical models.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, significantly reducing relaxation errors.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to mitigate dominant errors in neutral-atom quantum computing, enabling higher-fidelity gates and larger-scale devices.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally and numerically analyze a nonlinear cosφ coupling scheme to suppress these transitions, comparing with standard readout techniques.
result: The nonlinear coupling significantly reduces measurement-induced transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach offers a practical path to high-fidelity transmon readout, benefiting quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating decoherence is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and computation.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced single erbium emitters in silicon, using optical spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability and demonstrate improved coherence through cavity enhancement, achieving stable single-photon emission.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, advancing hybrid quantum systems for scalable quantum information processing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding how long-range interactions and kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phases, such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between cavity-mediated long-range interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phenomena in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring kinetically constrained dynamics and long-range interactions in cavity QED, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; a more efficient method is needed.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of k-local decoupling sequences.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, and can be tailored to device-specific noise correlations.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum computing platforms.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
