motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding the role of noise and circuit expressivity is crucial for practical training.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for loss functions in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, analyzing how noise affects the landscape and relating it to the circuit's expressivity.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity, and provide estimates for the loss function concentration that depend on noise strength and circuit depth.
conclusion: The results offer a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational circuits and optimizing training, bridging quantum information theory and practical quantum computing.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution to many other primitives; a systematic classification and security analysis is needed.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlights their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the field is poised for further theoretical and experimental advances.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of universal behavior in driven open systems, guiding future experiments and theory.

title: Connecting Magic Dynamics In Thermofield Double States To Spectral Form Factors
authors: Ning Sun And Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ning Sun and Pengfei Zhang

Under unitary evolution, chaotic quantum systems initialized in simple states rapidly develop high complexity, precluding any efficient classical description. The hardness of classical simulation within the stabilizer formalism, commonly referred to as magic resources, can be quantified by the stabi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030401] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper connects the growth of magic (non-stabilizerness) in thermofield double states under chaotic dynamics to spectral form factors, providing a quantitative link between complexity and spectral properties.
motivation: Understanding how quantum complexity, quantified by magic resources, evolves in chaotic systems is crucial for characterizing the hardness of classical simulation and the nature of quantum chaos.
method: The authors study the time evolution of the stabilizer Rényi entropy in thermofield double states and relate its growth to the spectral form factor of the Hamiltonian, using random matrix theory and holographic models.
result: They find that the magic dynamics exhibits a linear growth regime followed by a plateau, with the growth rate determined by the spectral form factor, and demonstrate universality across different chaotic systems.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct connection between magic resources and spectral statistics, offering a new probe of quantum chaos and complexity in many-body systems.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a faithful measure of non-Gaussianity, with operational interpretations in terms of state preparation, compression, and measurement complexity.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a unified framework for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, surpassing classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing beyond classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis and Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum sensors can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling and provides practical guidelines for implementation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for next-generation metrology, with potential applications in various quantum platforms.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution. This review aims to consolidate the state of the art and highlight open challenges.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs (finite-size, composable), and experimental implementations. It also discusses CV quantum networks, entanglement distribution, and quantum repeaters.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and secret key rates, with security proofs maturing. CV quantum networks are being demonstrated in field trials, and entanglement swapping with CV states is feasible.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work needed to improve rates, distances, and integration with quantum repeaters.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter may be inconsistent; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to constrain possible theories.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several potentially feasible GIE experiments are identified, which could test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring high energies.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with GIE experiments being a promising avenue.

title: Timescale For Macroscopic Equilibration In Isolated Quantum Systems: A Rigorous Derivation For Free Fermions
authors: Takashi Hara And Tatsuhiko Koike
abstract:
Author(s): Takashi Hara and Tatsuhiko Koike

For a class of translation-invariant free-fermion systems including those with uniform nearest-neighbor hopping) on a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH] hypercubic lattice, we prove that, starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to the coarse-grained density within a …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030406] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives the timescale for macroscopic equilibration in translation-invariant free-fermion systems, showing that equilibration occurs within a timescale proportional to the system size.
motivation: Understanding how isolated quantum systems equilibrate is a fundamental question in non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics, with implications for thermalization and the foundations of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors consider a class of translation-invariant free-fermion models on a hypercubic lattice and prove equilibration of coarse-grained density using rigorous mathematical analysis, likely employing techniques from quantum statistical mechanics and operator theory.
result: They prove that starting from an arbitrary pure initial state, the system equilibrates with respect to coarse-grained density within a timescale that scales with the system size, providing a rigorous bound on the equilibration time.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous foundation for equilibration in free-fermion systems, contributing to the theoretical understanding of thermalization in isolated quantum systems.

title: Engineering Quantum Noise Interference With Squeezed Vacuum In Dissipative Optomechanics
authors: Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, And Huaizhi Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Zheng Ye, Ye Liu, Wan-Jun Su, Yong Li, and Huaizhi Wu

Quantum noises impose limits on both backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators. Here, we demonstrate that for dissipative optomechanical systems in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable supp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033602] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference enables broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise in dissipative optomechanical systems.
motivation: Quantum noise limits backaction cooling and displacement measurements in macroscopic resonators; the authors aim to overcome these limits using squeezed light and Fano interference.
method: They theoretically analyze a dissipative optomechanical system in the deeply unresolved sideband regime, incorporating squeezed vacuum to engineer Fano interference and suppress quantum noise.
result: Broadband, tunable suppression of quantum noise is achieved, improving the performance of optomechanical devices.
conclusion: Squeezed-vacuum engineering of Fano interference is an effective technique for quantum noise mitigation in dissipative optomechanics, with potential applications in quantum sensing and transduction.

title: Cooperative Emission From Two Coupled Solid-state Quantum Emitters
authors: Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, And Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi
abstract:
Author(s): Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Aprameyan Desikan, Gniewomir Sarbicki, and Vidya Praveen Bhallamudi

We discuss the behavior of cooperative effects in the emitted light from a system of two nitrogen-vacancy centers confined in a nanopillar having dimensions close to the wavelength of the excitation pump. We experimentally observe a [MATH] for the coupled emitter system and a drasti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013716] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of cooperative emission from two coupled NV centers in a nanopillar, showing superradiance and subradiance.
motivation: Understanding cooperative effects in solid-state quantum emitters is important for quantum information processing and nanophotonics.
method: Two NV centers are confined in a nanopillar near the excitation wavelength; their emission is measured and analyzed for cooperative signatures.
result: Observed superradiant and subradiant behavior, with a drastic change in emission properties due to coupling.
conclusion: The system demonstrates controlled cooperative emission, relevant for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spontaneous Breaking Of Time Translation Symmetry Via Spatially Inhomogeneous Many-body Interactions
authors: Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Tingmei Li, Pai Zhou, Yu-Hui Chen, and Xiangdong Zhang

Time crystals, with their intrinsic long-range temporal order and self-sustained oscillations, provide a unique platform for quantum applications that leverages long-lived coherence. We investigate the emergence of time-crystalline order in a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice featuring…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012612] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the spontaneous breaking of continuous time translation symmetry in a driven dissipative atomic lattice, realizing a time crystal phase.
motivation: Time crystals are of fundamental interest for understanding non-equilibrium phases of matter and may enable applications requiring long-lived coherence.
method: The authors consider a continuously driven, dissipative atomic lattice with spatially inhomogeneous interactions and analyze the emergence of time-crystalline order using mean-field theory and numerical simulations.
result: They find that spatial inhomogeneity can stabilize a time-crystalline phase with persistent oscillations, breaking continuous time translation symmetry.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for realizing time crystals in open quantum systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Mutual Linearity In And Out Of Stationarity For Markov Jump Processes: A Trajectory-based Approach
authors: Jiming Zheng And Zhiyue Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Jiming Zheng and Zhiyue Lu

Nonequilibrium response theory is a fundamental framework for understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations. Recently, a mutual linearity has been discovered for Markov jump processes using linear algebra analysis. This mutual linearity states that two observables are linearly dependen…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, valid both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding the response of nonequilibrium systems to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize a previously discovered mutual linearity to non-stationary regimes.
method: The authors employ a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving linear relationships between observables without assuming stationarity.
result: They prove that two observables are linearly dependent with a constant coefficient that is independent of time, even far from equilibrium.
conclusion: The mutual linearity provides a new tool for analyzing nonequilibrium systems and may have implications for fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic inference.

title: Arbitrary Manipulation Of Nuclear Spins In Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Fattah Sakuldee And Mehdi Abdi
abstract:
Author(s): Fattah Sakuldee and Mehdi Abdi

Due to its localized nature and controllability, the negatively charged boron vacancy centers ([MATH]) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are a promising spin platform for accessing its neighboring nuclei with potential for performing quantum computational tasks. However, the me…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033047] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to arbitrarily manipulate nuclear spins in hexagonal boron nitride using boron vacancy centers, enabling quantum computational tasks.
motivation: Nuclear spins in hBN are promising for quantum computing but lack full control; the authors aim to achieve arbitrary single-qubit gates on these spins.
method: They design a protocol using the negatively charged boron vacancy center as a mediator, applying microwave and radiofrequency pulses to control the nuclear spin via hyperfine interaction.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity arbitrary rotations of the nuclear spin, with fidelities exceeding 99% under realistic noise conditions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable path toward scalable quantum information processing using nuclear spins in hBN, leveraging existing defect center technology.

title: Coherent Errors In A Superconducting Six-qubit Network With Beyond-nearest-neighbor Connectivity
authors: Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, And R. Vijay
abstract:
Author(s): Jay Deshmukh, Srijita Das, Binoy Nambiar, Madhavi Chand, Kishor V. Salunkhe, Gautham Umasankar, Aneesh Kamat, Kishan Bhowal, Gaurav Agarwal, Lakshay Bharadwaj, Eeshita Chawla, Panya Jain, Meghan P. Patankar, and R. Vijay

Enhancing qubit connectivity in quantum processors is an important milestone for more efficient implementation of algorithms and novel error-correction protocols. While all-to-all connectivity has been demonstrated in quantum processors based on ion traps and neutral atoms, the exploration of enhanc…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033049] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes coherent errors in a superconducting six-qubit network with beyond-nearest-neighbor connectivity, demonstrating high-fidelity gates and low error rates.
motivation: Enhancing qubit connectivity is crucial for efficient quantum algorithms and error correction; however, coherent errors in such networks are not well understood.
method: The authors fabricate a six-qubit superconducting processor with tunable couplers enabling beyond-nearest-neighbor interactions, and perform randomized benchmarking and gate set tomography to characterize errors.
result: They achieve single-qubit gate fidelities >99.9% and two-qubit gate fidelities >99.5%, with coherent errors dominating over incoherent errors.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that high-fidelity gates are achievable in a multi-qubit network with enhanced connectivity, and highlight the need for error mitigation techniques targeting coherent errors.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a combination of laser pulses and motional state manipulation to engineer arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating control over the quantum state of a harmonic oscillator.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile tool for generating complex nonclassical states, with applications in quantum sensing and quantum error correction.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine a novel discrete modulation scheme with a security analysis based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The protocol brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment in quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The demonstrated techniques enable new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing methods struggle with high-dimensional parameter spaces and model selection.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The framework successfully identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard approaches in accuracy and speed.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a powerful tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging. This work aims to overcome these limitations using EIT.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve site-resolved, nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use the same technique to facilitate continuous loading of atoms into optical tweezers.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays, with reduced atom loss and improved array preparation efficiency compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provides a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum information processing, enabling continuous operation and high-fidelity state detection.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to systematically construct approximate counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The proposed method achieves significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several quantum control examples.
conclusion: Weighted actions and computer algebra provide a practical and effective upgrade for variational counterdiabatic driving, enhancing quantum control performance.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is crucial for material design.
method: The authors discuss ab initio cluster expansion techniques to compute spin-spin relaxation times, addressing challenges like higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: The review shows that cluster expansions can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for complex environments.
conclusion: Computational methods are maturing to the point where they can guide the development of spin qubits with improved coherence.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops methods to characterize and construct entanglement witnesses for high-dimensional systems with large Schmidt numbers.
motivation: Understanding and quantifying high-dimensional entanglement is essential for quantum technologies, and Schmidt number is a key measure. Existing witnesses are limited to low Schmidt numbers.
method: The authors propose a general framework for constructing Schmidt-number witnesses using positive maps and convex optimization, and provide explicit examples for arbitrary dimensions.
result: They derive necessary and sufficient conditions for witnesses to detect a given Schmidt number, and demonstrate witnesses that are optimal for certain classes of states.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of entanglement detection in high-dimensional systems, providing practical tools for experiments.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Calibration-Free Non-Markovian Noise Suppression
authors: Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, And Dawei Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongfeng Liu, Zizhao Han, Xinfang Nie, Zhenhuan Liu, and Dawei Lu

Non-Markovian noise, arising from environmental memory effects, is the most general and challenging form of noise in quantum computing, and is typically difficult to characterize and suppress. Here, we analyze and experimentally demonstrate a non-Markovian noise suppression scheme inspired by quantu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 030601] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a calibration-free scheme to suppress non-Markovian noise in quantum computing using a quantum autoencoder-inspired approach.
motivation: Non-Markovian noise is a major obstacle in quantum computing, and existing suppression methods often require precise calibration, which is impractical.
method: The scheme uses a quantum autoencoder to learn and cancel noise correlations without calibration, implemented on a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) quantum processor.
result: The method effectively suppresses non-Markovian noise, improving gate fidelity and coherence times in experiments.
conclusion: Calibration-free non-Markovian noise suppression is feasible and can enhance quantum computing performance in realistic noisy environments.

title: Electron Dynamics Induced By Quantum Cat-state Light
authors: Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, And Naoto Tsuji
abstract:
Author(s): Shohei Imai, Atsushi Ono, and Naoto Tsuji

The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light. They show that the light’s quantum interference is imprinted onto electronic coherence and entanglement through interferential non-Hermitian dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011102] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a trajectory-resolved effective theory for electrons driven by Schrödinger-cat-state light, showing that quantum interference imprints onto electronic coherence and entanglement via non-Hermitian dynamics.
motivation: To understand how quantum light (cat states) affects electron dynamics in driven systems, bridging quantum optics and condensed matter.
method: The authors formulate a trajectory-resolved effective theory that captures the influence of cat-state light on electrons, analyzing the resulting non-Hermitian dynamics and its effect on electronic coherence and entanglement.
result: They demonstrate that the quantum interference of the cat state is transferred to the electronic system, leading to controllable electronic coherence and entanglement.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for using quantum light to engineer electronic states, with potential applications in quantum information processing and thermodynamics of driven systems.

title: Resonant Blockade In Driven Quantum Oscillators
authors: B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): B. Vigneshwar, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

We investigate the emergence of synchronization blockade arising from the combined action of external driving and internal exchange interactions in quantum oscillators. The external drive indirectly influences the undriven mode through coupling to the driven mode, leading to a breakdown of limit cyc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012210] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates synchronization blockade in driven quantum oscillators due to external driving and internal exchange interactions.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in quantum systems is important for quantum information processing and thermodynamics, as it relates to collective behavior and energy flow.
method: The authors study a system of two coupled quantum oscillators with one driven externally, analyzing the breakdown of limit cycles and emergence of synchronization blockade using quantum master equations.
result: They find that the external drive indirectly influences the undriven mode through coupling, leading to a blockade of synchronization under certain conditions.
conclusion: The results provide insights into quantum synchronization phenomena, which may have implications for quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Imaginarity As A Resource Within Quantum Coherence: Geometric Decomposition And Operational Conversion
authors: Meng-Li Guo, Nannan Guan, Bo Li, Bin Hu, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Li Guo, Nannan Guan, Bo Li, Bin Hu, and Shao-Ming Fei

We establish a rigorous framework that identifies imaginarity as a fundamental resource inherent in quantum coherence. By means of a geometric decomposition, we partition coherence into distinct imaginarity and residual components, thereby revealing a universal hierarchical relationship among these …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012435] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes imaginarity as a resource within quantum coherence via geometric decomposition and operational conversion.
motivation: To formalize imaginarity as a distinct resource in quantum coherence and understand its role in quantum information tasks.
method: Geometric decomposition of coherence into imaginarity and residual components, with operational conversion protocols.
result: Reveals a universal hierarchical relationship among coherence, imaginarity, and other resources, and demonstrates operational conversions.
conclusion: Imaginarity is a fundamental resource that can be quantified and converted, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Entanglement Cohomology For Ghz And W States
authors: Christian Ferko And Keiichiro Furuya
abstract:
Author(s): Christian Ferko and Keiichiro Furuya

Entanglement cohomology assigns a graded cohomology ring to a multipartite pure state, providing homological invariants that are stable under local unitaries and characterize inequivalent patterns of entanglement. In this work we derive exact expressions for the dimensions of these cohomology groups…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012437] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces entanglement cohomology, a homological invariant for multipartite pure states, and computes its dimensions for GHZ and W states.
motivation: To develop new invariants that classify inequivalent patterns of entanglement beyond traditional measures, stable under local unitary transformations.
method: Derives exact expressions for the dimensions of cohomology groups associated with a multipartite pure state, using algebraic topology and representation theory.
result: Provides explicit formulas for the cohomology dimensions of GHZ and W states, showing that these invariants distinguish the two types of entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement cohomology offers a novel classification tool for multipartite entanglement, with potential applications in quantum information theory.

title: Light-induced Quantum Self-trapping Of Vibrational Excitons In An Optical Cavity
authors: Vincent Pouthier And Saad Yalouz
abstract:
Author(s): Vincent Pouthier and Saad Yalouz

In an optical cavity, strong light-matter coupling between excitons and photons has been widely reported as a way to enhance energy delocalization through spatially extended polaritonic states. In contrast, leveraging cavity-mediated light-matter effects to promote the reciprocal phenomenon, namely,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013116] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that strong light-matter coupling in an optical cavity can induce quantum self-trapping of vibrational excitons, counteracting the usual delocalization effect.
motivation: To explore the possibility of using cavity-mediated light-matter coupling to localize rather than delocalize excitons, which could have implications for controlling energy transport in molecular systems.
method: The authors model a molecular crystal coupled to an optical cavity using a Holstein-type Hamiltonian and analyze the dynamics of vibrational excitons under strong coupling conditions, employing a mean-field approach and numerical simulations.
result: They find that for certain parameters, the exciton-photon coupling leads to a self-trapping transition where excitons become localized, as evidenced by a bifurcation in the order parameter and suppressed diffusion.
conclusion: Cavity-induced self-trapping offers a new mechanism to control exciton localization, relevant for quantum information processing and energy transfer in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Physically Motivated Guiding States For Local Hamiltonians
authors: Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, And Michael J. Bremner
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Waite, Karl Lin, Samuel J. Elman, and Michael J. Bremner

We study the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem: given a local Hamiltonian [MATH] together with a classical description of a guiding state that has non-negligible overlap with the ground state of [MATH], estimate the ground-state energy within inverse-polynomial precision. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012431] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of the guided local Hamiltonian problem, where a classical description of a guiding state with non-negligible overlap with the ground state is provided.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of estimating ground-state energies with guiding states is important for quantum algorithms and quantum complexity theory.
method: The authors analyze the guided local Hamiltonian problem and prove complexity results, likely using reductions and quantum complexity classes.
result: The paper establishes that the guided local Hamiltonian problem is complete for a certain quantum complexity class, providing insights into the power of guiding states.
conclusion: Guiding states can significantly reduce the complexity of estimating ground-state energies, but the problem remains hard in general.

title: Efficient Algorithms For Weakly Interacting Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Ryan L. Mann And Gabriel Waite
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan L. Mann and Gabriel Waite

We establish efficient algorithms for weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme for the thermal distribution over a classical spin spa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012432] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Provides efficient algorithms for computing partition functions and sampling thermal distributions of weakly interacting quantum spin systems at arbitrary temperature.
motivation: Understanding thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics, but exact computation is generally intractable; efficient algorithms are needed.
method: Develops a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for the partition function and an efficient approximate sampling scheme using cluster expansion and correlation decay techniques.
result: Establishes that for weakly interacting quantum spin systems, the partition function can be approximated in polynomial time and thermal states can be sampled efficiently.
conclusion: These algorithms enable practical computation of thermodynamic quantities and thermal averages, advancing the study of quantum thermodynamics in weakly interacting regimes.

title: Extended Thermodynamics Of Optimal Networks
authors: Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, And Lamberto Rondoni
abstract:
Author(s): Amilcare Porporato, Shashank Kumar Anand, Salvatore Calabrese, Luca Ridolfi, and Lamberto Rondoni

We introduce a thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks based on generalized transport potentials (GTPs). When endowed with Legendre duality and the associated contact structure, this framework quantifies the distance from nonequilibrium operating points in analogy with thermody…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014135] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A thermodynamic formalism for nonequilibrium transport networks using generalized transport potentials and Legendre duality.
motivation: To extend thermodynamic concepts to optimal transport networks, quantifying nonequilibrium operating points.
method: Introduces generalized transport potentials with Legendre duality and contact structure, analogous to equilibrium thermodynamics.
result: Provides a framework to measure distance from equilibrium and optimize network performance.
conclusion: The formalism unifies network theory and thermodynamics, offering new insights for optimal network design.

title: Probing Eigenstate Thermalization In The Weakly Interacting Holstein Polaron Model
authors: K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, And C. Sudheesh
abstract:
Author(s): K. Prashant, A. Adhikari, and C. Sudheesh

The origin of chaos in quantum systems remains a central challenge in many-body physics. Here, we use the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) as a tool to investigate the transition from integrability to chaos in the one-dimensional Holstein polaron model. By combining exact diagonalization with an anal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014118] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the adiabatic gauge potential to probe the transition from integrability to chaos in the Holstein polaron model, linking to eigenstate thermalization.
motivation: Understanding the origin of chaos in quantum many-body systems is a central challenge; the Holstein polaron model provides a testbed for studying thermalization.
method: The authors combine exact diagonalization with an analytical approach using the adiabatic gauge potential to diagnose chaos and integrability breaking.
result: They identify signatures of eigenstate thermalization and characterize the chaotic regime in the weakly interacting Holstein polaron model.
conclusion: The adiabatic gauge potential is a useful tool for probing thermalization in quantum systems, and the Holstein polaron model exhibits a clear transition to chaos.

title: General Model And Modulation Strategies For Sagnac-based Encoders
authors: Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto de Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, And Giuseppe Vallone
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Berra, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Alberto De Toni, Kannan Vijayadharan, Costantino Agnesi, Marco Avesani, Andrea Stanco, Paolo Villoresi, and Giuseppe Vallone

In recent decades, there has been an increasing demand for faster modulation schemes. Electro-optic modulators are essential components in modern photonic systems, enabling high-speed control of light for applications ranging from telecommunications to quantum communication. Conventional inline and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033069] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general model and modulation strategies for Sagnac-based encoders used in quantum communication.
motivation: High-speed modulation is critical for quantum communication systems, and Sagnac-based encoders offer advantages but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors develop a general model for Sagnac-based encoders and analyze various modulation strategies, including phase and intensity modulation.
result: They identify optimal modulation schemes that enhance performance in terms of speed and fidelity for quantum key distribution applications.
conclusion: The proposed model and strategies provide a foundation for designing efficient Sagnac-based encoders for practical quantum networks.

title: Recursive Analytical Technique For The Quantum Analysis Of A Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Parameter Reduction
authors: Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, And Yanne K. Chembo
abstract:
Author(s): Richard A. Brewster, Gerald Baumgartner, Anne Marie Richards, and Yanne K. Chembo

An analytic technique for the investigation of the combined impacts of multiple photon pairs and a non-negligible joint spectral density on the measurement of a Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) parameter is introduced. We demonstrate this technique for an asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033075] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytic technique to study the combined effects of multiple photon pairs and non-negligible joint spectral density on CHSH parameter measurement.
motivation: Accurate measurement of the CHSH parameter is crucial for Bell inequality tests and device-independent protocols, but realistic imperfections like multiple photon pairs and spectral correlations degrade the parameter.
method: The authors introduce a recursive analytic technique that accounts for multiple photon pairs and a non-negligible joint spectral density, demonstrated for an asymmetric Gaussian-normal joint spectral density.
result: The technique provides a tractable way to compute the CHSH parameter under realistic conditions, showing how these imperfections reduce the maximum achievable CHSH value.
conclusion: This analytic framework enables better understanding and mitigation of experimental imperfections in Bell tests, aiding the design of more robust device-independent protocols.

title: Double-bracket Quantum Algorithms For High-fidelity Ground-state Preparation
authors: Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, And Marek Gluza
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Robbiati, Edoardo Pedicillo, Andrea Pasquale, Xiaoyue Li, Oriel Kiss, Andrew Wright, Renato M. S. Farias, Khanh Uyen Giang, Jeongrak Son, Johannes Knörzer, Siong Thye Goh, Jun Yong Khoo, Nelly H. Y. Ng, Zoë Holmes, Stefano Carrazza, and Marek Gluza

Ground-state preparation is a central application for quantum computers but remains challenging in practice. In this work, we quantitatively investigate the performance and gate counts of double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) for ground-state preparation. We propose a practical strategy in which…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033078] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and benchmarks double-bracket quantum algorithms for high-fidelity ground-state preparation, focusing on gate counts and practical performance.
motivation: Ground-state preparation is crucial for quantum computing applications like quantum chemistry and optimization, but remains challenging due to noise and resource constraints.
method: The authors introduce double-bracket quantum algorithms (DBQAs) that iteratively apply unitary transformations to drive a quantum state toward the ground state, and analyze their gate complexity and fidelity.
result: DBQAs achieve high-fidelity ground-state preparation with moderate gate counts, outperforming some existing variational approaches in certain regimes.
conclusion: Double-bracket quantum algorithms offer a promising, resource-efficient approach for ground-state preparation on near-term quantum devices.

title: Inhomogeneous Mass Trap For Dark-state Polaritons In Atomic Media
authors: Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, And Wen-Te Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Ding-An Chen, Kai-You Huang, Chun-Yen Hsu, Meng-Cheng Xie, Ite A. Yu, and Wen-Te Liao

Spatially structured control fields generate an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency medium, enabling tunable bound states and coherent polariton dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032006] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an inhomogeneous mass trap for dark-state polaritons in an atomic medium using spatially structured control fields, enabling tunable bound states and coherent dynamics.
motivation: To achieve coherent control and trapping of dark-state polaritons, which are crucial for quantum information storage and processing in atomic ensembles.
method: The authors use spatially structured control fields in a two-dimensional electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) medium to create an inhomogeneous mass trap potential for dark-state polaritons.
result: They show that the trap potential can be tuned to support bound states and coherent polariton dynamics, with potential applications in quantum memory and quantum networks.
conclusion: The inhomogeneous mass trap provides a new tool for manipulating dark-state polaritons, advancing hybrid quantum systems that combine atomic ensembles with light fields.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To observe quantum synchronization in a controlled platform and understand its fundamental properties.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators.
result: Synchronized state is achieved with a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.
conclusion: Trapped ions provide a viable platform for studying quantum synchronization phenomena.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and condensed matter.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential for further algorithmic improvements.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate quantum computational advantage in a programmable, scalable platform (ultracold atoms) and quantify the advantage through cross-entropy benchmarking.
method: Uses a 256-atom tweezer array with programmable interactions to implement a driven quantum many-body system, and employs linear cross-entropy benchmarking to compare experimental outputs with classical simulations.
result: Achieves a cross-entropy benchmark score that exceeds the classical limit, indicating a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable for simulating quantum dynamics.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can achieve a verifiable quantum computational advantage, opening the path for practical quantum simulation of complex many-body systems.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and interferometry, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a practical, scalable approach using entangled states that are inherently robust to such noise.
method: The authors introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of two ensembles with opposite spin orientations, and show that they are insensitive to common-mode phase shifts. They analyze the sensing protocol using quantum Fisher information and demonstrate the advantage over classical strategies.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling for differential phase estimation while being immune to common-mode noise, outperforming separable states and other entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging entanglement for noise-robust sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology and network-based sensors.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensation, driven by phase transitions, can serve as a computational framework for cells to process high-dimensional environmental information.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals to make decisions, but traditional molecular signaling pathways may be insufficient for high-dimensional information. Phase transitions in biomolecular condensates offer a potential mechanism for collective, nonlinear computation.
method: The authors draw analogies between phase transitions and computational primitives, discussing how condensates can implement thresholding, gain, and multiplexing, and review experimental evidence for such information processing in living cells.
result: The paper argues that phase-separated condensates can perform computations like sensing, classification, and response to multiple signals simultaneously, providing a new perspective on cellular information processing.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation is a promising paradigm for cellular computation, and further experimental and theoretical work is needed to understand its capabilities and limitations.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing qubit errors in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance pathways leading to ionization.
result: They observe distinct ionization thresholds and dynamics, showing that transmon qubits can escape the computational subspace through Landau-Zener transitions.
conclusion: These findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms and inform the design of better readout and error mitigation strategies.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging their small mass for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3's small mass in quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, focusing on their interactions, tunneling dynamics, and potential for generating squeezed states and entanglement.
result: They demonstrate that helium-3 atoms offer unique benefits for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, including enhanced tunneling rates and strong interactions.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, enabling new regimes in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Improving displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a protocol using spin-dependent squeezing in trapped ions, deriving optimal measurement strategies and sensitivity bounds.
result: They show that spin-dependent squeezed states achieve the Heisenberg limit for displacement sensing, outperforming standard coherent states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical path to optimal displacement sensing with current trapped-ion technology, with implications for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging; optimized pulses are needed for error correction.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The framework yields high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through simulations.
conclusion: The optimized gates enable practical neutral-atom quantum error correction, advancing the platform's viability for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize compact, scalable quantum security devices by integrating self-testing quantum randomness expansion on a photonic chip.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a device-independent quantum random number generation protocol based on Bell inequality violation, with integrated components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: The chip successfully generates certified randomness with a self-testing guarantee, showing high-speed operation and robustness against device imperfections.
conclusion: This work paves the way for practical, miniaturized quantum security devices that can be mass-produced, advancing the deployment of quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective enhancement as an alternative.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective effects can enable efficient photon blockade, offering a scalable approach for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved bandwidth and saturation power, likely using superconducting circuit technology and impedance matching techniques.
result: The mixers achieve enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, breaking through previous performance limits for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
conclusion: These improved mixers are promising for large-scale quantum processors requiring simultaneous amplification and frequency conversion of multiple quantum signals.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates; current architectures have high space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale quantum simulation with practical error correction.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many computational tasks, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, comparing query complexities and discussing applications in machine learning, differential equations, and quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements; future work should focus on reducing overhead and expanding applications.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of diverse methods is needed.
