Here, we introduce a superradiant parametric Mössbauer radiation (SPMR) source, which utilizes the scattering of spatially microstructured e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 035001] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a superradiant parametric Mössbauer radiation source for generating high-flux x-ray pulses using microstructured targets and nuclear resonances.
motivation: Future applications of Mössbauer nuclei require x-ray sources with exceptionally high peak and average spectral flux, which are not achievable with current sources.
method: The authors introduce a scheme where spatially microstructured targets are used to scatter x-rays, inducing superradiant emission from Mössbauer nuclei via parametric down-conversion-like processes.
result: The proposed source can produce coherent, narrow-band x-ray pulses with significantly enhanced flux compared to conventional Mössbauer sources.
conclusion: This work provides a path toward practical high-flux x-ray sources for nuclear resonance applications, though it is primarily an experimental physics proposal without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kondo Effect In Nonreciprocal Response
authors: Hajime Murata And Hiroaki Ishizuka
abstract:

Chiral magnetic states give rise to rich phenomena, from the anomalous Hall effect and the nonlinear electrical current to multiferroics and magnetochiral dichroism. Most of the studies on electrical transport so far have focused on the cases where the magnetic moments are well approximated by class…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036301] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Kondo effect in nonreciprocal transport in chiral magnets, focusing on electrical transport phenomena.
motivation: Chiral magnetic states exhibit rich transport phenomena, but the role of the Kondo effect in nonreciprocal response is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the Kondo effect in a chiral magnet using a microscopic model and calculate the nonreciprocal conductivity.
result: They find that the Kondo effect can significantly enhance nonreciprocal response under certain conditions.
conclusion: The Kondo effect is an important mechanism for nonreciprocal transport in chiral magnets, offering new insights into magnetochiral phenomena.

title: Nonlinear Odd Viscoelastic Effect

Nonlinear odd viscoelastic effects arise from higher-order quantum geometric tensors in magnetic three-dimensional topological phases in response to distortion fields.

method: The authors derive nonlinear viscoelastic response functions from higher-order quantum geometric tensors in magnetic 3D topological phases.
result: They identify odd viscoelastic effects that are nonlinear and originate from quantum geometry.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of viscoelastic phenomena in topological phases, but it is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Even Denominator Fractional Quantum Hall States In The Zeroth Landau Level Of Aba Trilayer Graphene
authors: Tanima Chanda, Simrandeep Kaur, Harsimran Singh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Manish Jain, Udit Khanna, Ajit C. Balram, And Aveek Bid

Even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at half-filling are of particular interest because they can host non-Abelian quasiparticles. tldr: This paper reports the observation of even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states in the zeroth Landau level of ABA trilayer graphene, which are of interest for hosting non-Abelian quasiparticles.
motivation: Even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states are of particular interest because they can host non-Abelian quasiparticles, which are important for topological quantum computation. The zeroth Landau level in trilayer graphene was previously thought to be unpolarized, making such states unexpected.
method: The authors performed transport measurements on ABA trilayer graphene devices at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, and analyzed the longitudinal and Hall resistances to identify fractional quantum Hall states.
result: They observed even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at half-filling in the zeroth Landau level, challenging the conventional expectation that such states are absent in this system.
conclusion: The observation of these states in trilayer graphene provides a new platform for studying non-Abelian quasiparticles and may have implications for topological quantum computation.

motivation: To search for violations of Lorentz and CPT symmetry in deuterium, which could indicate physics beyond the Standard Model.
method: Hyperfine spectroscopy of two transitions in ground-state deuterium, searching for sidereal variations in transition frequencies.
result: Constraints on nonrelativistic proton coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension were obtained, but no significant violations were found.
conclusion: The experiment sets improved limits on certain symmetry-violating coefficients, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Commensurate-Incommensurate Mott Transition Without Magnetic Field: Emergence Of Nematic Luttinger Liquid In Xxz Chain

tldr: This paper studies the zero magnetization ground state phase diagram of a spin-1/2 XXZ chain with competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions, revealing a nematic Luttinger liquid phase.
motivation: To understand the emergence of nematic order in spin chains without external magnetic fields, which is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics.
method: Uses density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations to compute the ground state phase diagram.
result: Identifies a commensurate-incommensurate Mott transition and a nematic Luttinger liquid phase in the strongly interacting regime.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into quantum phases in frustrated spin chains, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Pseudochiral Phonons From Octupolar Magnetic Order
authors: Ruairidh Sutcliffe, Kathleen Hart, Swati Chaudhary, And Arun Paramekanti

motivation: Recent discovery of large magnetic response of chiral phonons in dipolar magnets motivates exploring similar effects in multipolar magnets.
method: The authors consider Raman active quantum phonons in multipolar magnets and analyze their pseudochiral properties using theoretical models.
result: They show that pseudochiral phonons emerge in octupolar magnetic order, leading to anomalous magnetic responses.
conclusion: Pseudochiral phonons provide a new avenue for studying magneto-phononic effects in multipolar magnets.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of Superfluidity And Shear Rigidity In Different Phases Of A Dipolar Bose-Einstein Condensate
authors: Soumyadeep Halder, Hari Sadhan Ghosh, Axel Pelster, And B. Prasanna Venkatesh

tldr: This paper studies dynamical signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate by suddenly changing the polarization direction of magnetic dipole moments.
motivation: To probe superfluid and solid-like properties in dipolar BECs using a sudden change in polarization direction as a dynamical probe.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the response of a dipolar BEC to a sudden small angular deviation of the polarization direction, examining the resulting dynamics.
result: They find that the dynamical response reveals signatures of superfluidity and shear rigidity in different phases of the dipolar BEC.
conclusion: The sudden polarization change serves as a useful probe to distinguish superfluid and solid-like phases in dipolar BECs.

title: Spin-orbit-coupling-induced Geometric Squeezing In Rotating Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Fei Zhu, Chunxia Guo, Rui Zhang, Lianghui Huang, Ren Zhang, And Li Chen

Squeezed states play a key role in diverse frontiers of quantum physics. Geometrically squeezed states, squeezed states in the orbital phase space of rotating Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), have been conventionally generated by anisotropic-trapping potentials. In this work, we propose a different…

tldr: This paper proposes generating geometric squeezed states in rotating Bose-Einstein condensates via spin-orbit coupling instead of anisotropic trapping.
motivation: Geometric squeezing in rotating BECs is conventionally achieved with anisotropic traps; this work explores an alternative mechanism using spin-orbit coupling.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a rotating BEC with spin-orbit coupling, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and calculating the squeezing parameter.
result: Spin-orbit coupling can induce geometric squeezing in the orbital phase space, offering a new control knob for squeezed state generation.

tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of nonlinear spin dynamics in dual-cell atomic gases, focusing on spin masers and time crystals.

title: Electric Dipole Spin-flip Resonances In Semiconductors: A Personal Perspective
authors: Bruce D. Mccombe
abstract:
Author(s): Bruce D. McCombe

Emmanuel Rashba is responsible for a body of theory that demonstrates the profound effects of spin-orbit interaction on charge carriers in semiconductors. This notably includes the discovery of important effects on confined carriers in the presence of structural inversion asymmetry. The present article describes, from a personal perspective, experimental discovery and studies of electric-field-excited spin-flip resonances in semiconductors motivated by these theoretical predictions. Initial experiments in 1960 focused on electric-dipole excited spin resonance (EDSR) and combined cyclotron plus spin resonance (in 1967). Recent experiments on quasi-two-dimensional electrons in the quantum Hall effect regime in an asymmetric quantum-well structure have revealed unusual multiline EDSR spectra attributed to effects of Rashba spin-orbit effective fields of electrons in quantum Hall edge channels.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 019603] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: A personal perspective on experimental studies of electric-dipole spin-flip resonances in semiconductors, motivated by Rashba's theory.
motivation: To provide a historical account of experimental discoveries of electric-field-excited spin-flip resonances in semiconductors, driven by Rashba's theoretical predictions.
method: Review of experimental studies from 1960 onward, including EDSR and combined cyclotron plus spin resonance, with recent experiments on quasi-2D electrons in asymmetric quantum wells.
result: Discovery of unusual multiline EDSR spectra attributed to Rashba spin-orbit effective fields in quantum Hall edge channels.
conclusion: The work highlights the lasting impact of Rashba's theory on experimental semiconductor physics, but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Theory Of Next-generation Even-denominator States
authors: Misha Yutushui And David F. Mross
abstract:
Author(s): Misha Yutushui and David F. Mross

Here, the authors establish a comprehensive theory for the recently observed “next-generation” even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states and reveal that they are topologically equivalent to Bonderson-Slingerland phases. They present numerical simulations showing significant and systematic microscopic differences between the two families of states: next-generation states are favored in the lowest Landau level, while Bonderson-Slingerland states are favored in the first excited level. Finally, the authors prove that essential universal properties of topological edges are preserved under flux attachment and leverage this result to predict experimental signatures of next-generation even-denominator states.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065121] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory for next-generation even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states, showing they are topologically equivalent to Bonderson-Slinger phases but with different microscopic origins.
motivation: Recent experiments observed new even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states that do not fit existing theories, motivating a comprehensive theoretical understanding.
method: The authors use topological field theory and numerical simulations to compare next-generation states with Bonderson-Slinger phases, and prove that universal properties of topological edges are preserved under flux attachment.
result: Next-generation states are favored in the lowest Landau level while Bonderson-Slinger states are favored in the first excited level; essential universal properties of topological edges are preserved under flux attachment.
conclusion: The theory predicts experimental signatures that can distinguish next-generation even-denominator states from other candidates.

tldr: This paper studies the effective long-range attraction of moiré excitons in twisted transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers, focusing on atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening.

method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening to compute the effective potential between interlayer excitons in twisted TMD bilayers.
result: They find that atomic reconstructions and anisotropic screening can lead to an effective long-range attraction between moiré excitons, which may facilitate the formation of exciton condensates or other correlated states.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of structural and screening effects in moiré systems and suggests new avenues for engineering exciton interactions.

method: The authors develop a generalized framework for the ferroelectric controlled nonlinear Hall effect, likely using band structure calculations and symmetry analysis.

authors: Xinliang Lyu

method: The tensor-network renormalization group (TNRG) algorithm is used to analyze the hard-square lattice gas model, incorporating lattice and PT symmetries.

result: They observe twofold degenerate acoustic Landau levels and demonstrate pseudospin-dependent transport, confirming the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of Landau levels to classical acoustic systems and may enable new wave manipulation devices.

title: Beyond The Arcsine Law: Aging Statistics Of The Occupation Time In Jump Processes
authors: Arthur Plaud And Olivier Bénichou
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Plaud and Olivier Bénichou

Occupation times quantify how long a stochastic process remains in a region, and their single-time statistics are famously given by the arcsine law for Brownian and Lévy processes. By contrast, two-time occupation statistics—which directly probe temporal correlations and aging—have resisted exact ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014137] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, revealing aging behavior beyond the classical arcsine law.
motivation: Occupation times are fundamental in stochastic processes, but two-time statistics—which probe temporal correlations and aging—have not been exactly characterized for jump processes.
method: The authors derive exact expressions for the joint distribution of occupation times at two different times for a class of jump processes, using renewal theory and Laplace transform methods.

conclusion: The work extends the understanding of occupation time statistics to aging phenomena in jump processes, with potential applications in physics and biology where such processes model transport.

title: Finite-size Scaling To Resolve Spurious Multifractality In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, And Maria Cristina Mariani

conclusion: Finite-size scaling is essential to avoid misinterpretation of multifractal analysis in spin systems.

result: The PRG signatures in neuronal models are not as robust as in equilibrium critical systems, questioning the interpretation of criticality in the brain.
conclusion: Caution is needed when interpreting PRG results as evidence for criticality in neuronal systems.

motivation: Finding optimal paths in fluid flows is important for autonomous vehicles and active particles, but the problem is challenging when the agent's speed is comparable to the flow speed.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a time-optimal control problem and apply reinforcement learning to compute optimal trajectories in various flow fields.
result: They demonstrate that the reinforcement learning approach successfully finds near-optimal paths, outperforming traditional methods in complex flows.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning is an effective tool for solving navigation problems in fluid flows, with potential applications in robotics and oceanography.

result: Bias acts as a competing mechanism that can weaken or suppress localization, altering the stationary state distribution.
conclusion: The competition between bias and resetting leads to a localization-delocalization transition, with implications for transport and search processes.

result: Observation of various collective behaviors including incoherent activity, coherent traveling waves, and chimera states.
conclusion: Electric fields can induce complex spatiotemporal patterns in thermosensitive neuronal networks, relevant to neuroscience but not to quantum information theory.

result: They derive stability conditions for twisted states and show that adaptive feedback can stabilize or destabilize certain twisted states depending on parameters.

title: Energy-dynamics Interplay In Temporal Networks Triggers Explosive Synchronization
authors: Romuald Mbonwouo, Steve J. Kongni, Sishu Shankar Muni, Carmel T. Lambu, Venceslas Nguefoue, Patrick Louodop, And Thierry Njougouo

Synchronization in networks of coupled oscillators is a fundamental problem in the study of collective behavior. In this paper we investigate the synchronization transition in networks of coupled dynamical systems from an energetic perspective. Interactions between systems/oscillators are assumed to…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014210] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies explosive synchronization in temporal networks from an energetic perspective, focusing on coupled oscillators and collective behavior.
motivation: Understanding synchronization transitions in networks is fundamental to collective behavior, and an energetic perspective may reveal new mechanisms.
method: The authors model interactions between coupled dynamical systems with temporal network structures and analyze synchronization transitions using energy-based measures.
result: They find that the interplay between energy dynamics and temporal network structure triggers explosive synchronization.
conclusion: The work provides insights into synchronization phenomena but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, and Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for combinatorial reasoning in large language models, using a quantum computer to solve a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with complex reasoning tasks that require combinatorial optimization; quantum computers may offer advantages for such problems.
method: The authors reformulate reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization (HUBO) problem and solve it using a real quantum computer integrated into a hybrid workflow.
result: The framework demonstrates improved reasoning accuracy on selected benchmarks compared to classical baselines, leveraging quantum optimization.
conclusion: Quantum combinatorial reasoning can enhance LLM performance on structured reasoning tasks, though practical scalability remains a challenge.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays
authors: Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, And J. V. Alvarez
abstract:
Author(s): Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, and J. V. Alvarez

Rotating colloids, or spinners, in obstacle arrays exhibit frequency-set stationary orbits and currents set by the competition between an inertial, Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction. Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations reveal the hydrodynamic coupling and identify the lift mechani…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033071] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transport of rotating colloids in obstacle arrays using lattice-Boltzmann simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic lift and particle trajectories.
motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and active matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to model rotating colloids in obstacle arrays, capturing hydrodynamic interactions and lift forces.
result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents arising from the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of spinners in structured media, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials
authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka
abstract:
Author(s): Alireza Jozani and Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares three proposals for computing detection time distributions in quantum mechanics using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are multiple inequivalent proposals for the probability distribution of detection times, and a systematic comparison is needed to understand their differences and implications.
method: The authors compute detection time distributions for three proposals: two based on absorbing boundary conditions and one based on imaginary potentials, and compare them analytically and numerically.
result: The three proposals yield different distributions, highlighting the lack of consensus on the correct quantum arrival time distribution.
conclusion: Further theoretical and experimental work is needed to determine which proposal, if any, correctly describes detection times in quantum mechanics.

title: Mie-tronics Supermodes And Symmetry Breaking In Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, And Yuri Kivshar
abstract:

It is usually believed that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement, such as in the case of metasurfaces when bound states in the continuum are replaced by quasibound states with lower quality [MATH] factors. Here, in contrast, we reveal that symmetry breaking can instead en…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033076] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies symmetry breaking in nonlocal metasurfaces, revealing that it can enhance light confinement via Mie-tronics supermodes.
motivation: To challenge the conventional belief that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement and lower Q factors.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically analyze nonlocal metasurfaces, demonstrating that symmetry breaking can create supermodes with enhanced confinement.
result: Symmetry breaking in Mie-tronic metasurfaces can lead to stronger light confinement and higher Q factors, contrary to typical expectations.
conclusion: This work provides a new mechanism for controlling light confinement in metasurfaces, with potential applications in nanophotonics.

title: Quantum-classical Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo With Matchgate Shadows On Trapped Ion Quantum Computers

We demonstrate an end-to-end workflow to model chemical reaction barriers with the quantum-classical auxiliary field quantum Monte Carlo (QC-AFQMC) algorithm with quantum tomography using matchgate shadows. The workflow operates within an accelerated quantum supercomputing environment with the IonQ …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033061] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum-classical hybrid algorithm for quantum chemistry using matchgate shadows on trapped ion quantum computers.

title: Shell Formation And Two-dimensional Nanofriction In Three-dimensional Ion Coulomb Crystals
authors: L. A. Rüffert And T. E. Mehlstäubler
abstract:

Self-organized three-dimensional (3D) ion Coulomb crystals in linear Paul traps naturally form concentric shells that provide a curved, atomically resolved interface for studying two-dimensional (2D) nanofriction. Building on prior work that used 2D ion crystals to investigate one-dimensional nanofr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033044] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shell formation and nanofriction in 3D ion Coulomb crystals, which is a topic in classical or mesoscopic physics with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding nanofriction at curved interfaces using ion crystals as a model system.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of shell structures in 3D ion Coulomb crystals in a linear Paul trap.
result: Observation of concentric shells and measurement of nanofriction between them.
conclusion: Ion Coulomb crystals provide a platform for studying two-dimensional nanofriction.

title: Kramers Dichroism In $PT$-symmetric Magnets
authors: Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, And Justin C. W. Song
abstract:
Author(s): Oles Matsyshyn, Ying Xiong, and Justin C. W. Song

The quantum states in doubly degenerate Kramers pairs can act as an internal degree of freedom. Here, we uncover a Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets: interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light irradiation can selectively polarize Kramers partnered states allowing to control …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033046] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kramers dichroism in PT-symmetric magnets, a condensed matter phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how circularly polarized light can selectively polarize Kramers pairs in PT-symmetric magnets, potentially enabling control of internal degrees of freedom.
method: The authors theoretically analyze interband transitions induced by circularly polarized light in PT-symmetric magnets, using symmetry arguments and band structure calculations.
result: They uncover a Kramers dichroism effect where circularly polarized light selectively excites one Kramers partner over the other, leading to a net polarization.
conclusion: This effect provides a mechanism to control Kramers pairs optically, which may be useful for spintronics or other applications, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-normal Eigenvector Amplification In Multidimensional Kesten Processes
authors: Virgile Troude And Didier Sornette
abstract:
Author(s): Virgile Troude and Didier Sornette

Heavy-tailed fluctuations and power law statistics pervade physics, finance, and economics, yet their origin is often ascribed to systems poised near criticality. Here, we show that such behavior can emerge far from instability through a universal mechanism of non-normal eigenvector amplification in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033050] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that heavy-tailed fluctuations can arise from non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes, far from criticality.
motivation: To explain the origin of heavy-tailed statistics in complex systems without invoking criticality.
method: Analyzes non-normal eigenvector amplification in multidimensional Kesten processes using random matrix theory and stochastic recurrence equations.
result: Demonstrates that non-normality can generate power-law distributions even when the spectral radius is less than one.
conclusion: Non-normal amplification provides a universal mechanism for heavy tails in systems far from instability.

title: Anisotropic Interactions Induce Dynamical Spin Freezing In Artificial Colloidal Ice
authors: Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú And Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo G. Alanis-Cantú and Antonio Ortiz-Ambriz

Artificial colloidal ice is an icelike system used to study the effects of frustration in controlled environments, where all degrees of freedom can be accessed at a length scale large enough for optical visualization and in real time. We modify this model system by inducing anisotropic interactions …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033051] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical spin freezing in artificial colloidal ice with anisotropic interactions, a classical statistical mechanics system.
motivation: To understand how anisotropic interactions affect frustration and dynamics in artificial spin ice systems.
method: Experimental realization of artificial colloidal ice with tunable anisotropic interactions via optical traps, combined with video microscopy and analysis of spin configurations.
result: Anisotropic interactions induce a dynamical freezing transition where spins become trapped in metastable configurations.
conclusion: Anisotropy can control relaxation dynamics in frustrated systems, offering insights into glassy behavior.

title: Ultracold Amplification Proposal For Parity Violation In Chiral Molecules
authors: Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, And Salvador Miret-Artés
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Martínez-Gil, Pedro Bargueño, and Salvador Miret-Artés

We propose a theoretical mechanism to indirectly detect the small parity-violating energy difference (PVED) between chiral enantiomers through a macroscopic enantiomeric excess observed in an ultracold gas. We consider that chiral molecules are formed resonantly via ultracold collisions of achiral d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033056] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a theoretical mechanism to detect parity violation in chiral molecules via ultracold gas amplification.
motivation: Parity-violating energy differences in chiral molecules are extremely small and have not been directly observed; the authors aim to amplify this effect to detectable levels.
method: They model ultracold collisions of achiral fragments that resonantly form chiral molecules, and analyze the resulting enantiomeric excess due to parity violation.
result: The mechanism predicts a macroscopic enantiomeric excess that could be measured experimentally, providing indirect evidence of parity violation.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable path to observe parity violation in chiral molecules using ultracold chemistry.

title: Moiré-resonant Surface State In Ultrathin ${\mathrm{RuO}}_{2}(110)$
authors: Philipp Keßler, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Armando Consiglio, Hendrik Hohmann, Ronny Thomale, Jonas Erhardt, Bing Liu, Vedran Jovic, Ralph Claessen, Patrick Härtl, Matteo Dürrnagel, And Simon Moser

method: The authors use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) to characterize the electronic structure.
result: They observe moiré-resonant surface states and discuss the role of dimensional quenching and electron correlations.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the surface electronic properties of RuO2, relevant for altermagnetic thin films.

title: Topological States And Flat Bands In Exactly Solvable Decorated Cayley Trees
authors: Wanda P. Duss, Askar Iliasov, And Tomáš Bzdušek
abstract:

We derive the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that constitute tree analogs of selected two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, namely, the Lieb, the double-Lieb, the kagome, and the star lattice. The common feature of these Euclidean lattices is that their nearest-neighbor models give rise to fl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033036] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the full spectrum of decorated Cayley trees that are tree analogs of certain two-dimensional Euclidean lattices, revealing flat bands and topological states.
motivation: To understand the spectral properties and topological features of tree-like structures that mimic flat-band lattices.
method: Exact diagonalization and analytical derivation of the spectrum for decorated Cayley trees corresponding to Lieb, double-Lieb, kagome, and star lattices.
result: The spectra exhibit flat bands and topological edge states analogous to those in the Euclidean lattices.
conclusion: Decorated Cayley trees serve as tractable models for studying flat-band physics and topological states in non-Euclidean geometries.

title: Topology And Geometry Of Clusters In The Vicsek Model Across Scales
authors: Ashiqur Rahman, Michael Napoli, Ofek Lauber Bonomo, Maurizio Porfiri, And Nicole Abaid

Collective motion in active matter can arise from interaction rules that generate group-level order. A seminal example is the Vicsek model, which describes flocking using a simple local alignment rule. Despite three decades of research, the network topology induced by the particles’ alignment remain…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033039] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the topology and geometry of clusters in the Vicsek model of collective motion across different scales.
motivation: Understanding how local alignment rules in active matter systems lead to emergent collective behavior is a fundamental question in statistical physics.
method: The authors analyze the network topology induced by particle alignment in the Vicsek model, examining cluster properties across scales using computational simulations.
result: They characterize the topological and geometric features of clusters, revealing scale-dependent behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the structure of collective motion but do not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Emergence Of Bistability And Even-order Harmonic Generation In A Centrosymmetric System Under Periodic Driving

motivation: To explore emergent non-equilibrium properties in periodically driven systems that are absent in equilibrium.
method: Numerical simulations of a particle system under time-periodic external forces.
result: Observation of bistability and even-order harmonic generation in a centrosymmetric system.
conclusion: Periodic driving can induce exotic dynamical behaviors in centrosymmetric systems.

title: Quantum Physics-informed Neural Network With Residual-based Adaptive Refinement For Solving Partial Differential Equations
authors: Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, And Zhichao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Le Li, Junkai Yang, Qingle Wang, and Zhichao Zhang

In this paper, we propose a quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by using residual-based adaptive refinement (RAR). The method incorporates a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism into the training of QPINN, which aims to enhance conver…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033042] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum physics-informed neural network with residual-based adaptive refinement for solving partial differential equations.
motivation: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are powerful for solving PDEs but suffer from convergence issues; quantum neural networks may offer advantages.
method: A quantum neural network is trained with a residual-driven adaptive sampling mechanism (RAR) to focus on regions with high PDE residuals.
result: The QPINN with RAR achieves improved accuracy and convergence compared to standard PINNs on benchmark PDEs.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks combined with adaptive sampling can effectively solve PDEs, but the work is primarily a numerical method without deep quantum information or thermodynamics insights.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:

tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They introduce Floquet amplitude modulations into the analog Floquet solver to help the system escape local minima.
result: The proposed method significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator-based Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet-based Ising machines with amplitude modulations are an effective approach for escaping local minima in combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayers.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter combining topology and strong correlations, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy is used to measure the out-of-plane magneto-optical response of a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: An out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response is observed, consistent with a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings provide experimental support for the existence of fractional topological insulators, opening a new direction in condensed matter physics.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum theory with general relativity without quantizing gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum mechanics and classical gravity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable framework for whether spacetime needs a quantum description.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral formalism that couples quantum fields to a classical spacetime background, incorporating backreaction effects.
result: A consistent mathematical framework is presented that describes the dynamics of quantum fields on a classical spacetime with backreaction, potentially enabling experimental tests of the classical nature of spacetime.
conclusion: The work offers a novel approach to the quantum-gravity problem that avoids full quantization of gravity, with implications for testing the quantumness of spacetime.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring physics models, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific discovery process, but the paper is a demonstration of AI methodology rather than a contribution to the specific research directions listed.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob

result: The study identifies that rare cage escapes are the primary drivers of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs only applied to the dilute regime, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime; this gap needed to be bridged.
method: The authors prove that approximate sampling from the output distribution of linear-optical interferometers with a linear number of modes is hard for classical computers under standard complexity assumptions, using techniques from random matrix theory and anticoncentration.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard, even in the presence of noise, and provide evidence that the output distribution is anticoncentrated.
conclusion: This work validates the complexity-theoretic basis for current photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantization of chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, with detection via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations that may exhibit novel quantum behavior.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their low-energy excitations and scattering properties.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for observing quantum chiral solitons in experiments, linking soliton dynamics to Luttinger liquid physics.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:

method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative discretization of the sphere, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs, and analyze the spectrum and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory, and compute scaling dimensions and operator content.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a powerful numerical tool for studying strongly coupled CFTs, and the observed emergent supersymmetry suggests deeper theoretical structures.
