title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To develop a general method for predicting physical links in networks based on observed dynamics.
method: The authors propose a framework that leverages physical principles to infer causal relationships from time-series data of networked systems.
result: The framework successfully identifies causal links across various network dynamics, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: The approach provides a powerful tool for understanding and predicting interactions in complex networks.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods to study anyon superfluidity.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transitions in frustrated magnetic systems, specifically kagome spin ice HoAgGe.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other characterization techniques.
result: Observation of a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and evidence for hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the exotic magnetic phases of kagome spin ice materials.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but most are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and characterize their electronic structure using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: This material system offers a promising avenue for exploring flat-band physics and strongly correlated phenomena at practical temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic phases.
result: A spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase is observed, and electric-field control enables transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and simulations to investigate the liquid-vapor critical point of a model hyperuniform fluid composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit unique critical phenomena that may have implications for materials design and fundamental statistical mechanics.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different types of order parameters (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material and the formation of complex domain walls.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were applied to Ni₂MnSbO₆ to identify and distinguish the different orders.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The study reveals a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational components, which may have implications for understanding complex order parameters in solids.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each representing a key milestone in quantum computing development.
result: A roadmap for quantum computing utility is presented, but no new technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on quantum computing progress but does not advance specific technical directions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is believed to be a classically hard problem that quantum computers can solve efficiently.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and demonstrating the potential for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides evidence that quantum algorithms can outperform classical methods for certain topological computations.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with broad fundamental and applied implications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in both optical and acoustic waves, and review experimental demonstrations.
result: They show that optical and acoustic forces and torques can be described within a unified formalism, highlighting phenomena such as pulling forces and spin-induced torques.
conclusion: The unified perspective provides a comprehensive understanding of wave-matter interactions, with potential applications in particle trapping, sorting, and manipulation.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on their exotic electronic states and many-body phenomena.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual states in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and orbital antiferromagnetism.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and correlation effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects.
conclusion: Kagome metals host a rich variety of exotic states due to geometric frustration and electronic correlations.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex systems, but a unified field-theoretic framework is lacking.
method: The authors review and unify various field-theoretic approaches, including Doi-Peliti formalism and path integrals, for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unifying framework for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational-wave and X-ray measurements.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is important for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Review of observational data from gravitational-wave events (binary neutron star mergers) and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to theoretical nuclear equation of state models.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are summarized, showing consistency with some nuclear models but leaving uncertainties at high densities.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state, but current data already provide important insights into dense matter.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological characteristics of Kitaev spin liquids.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with significant implications for condensed matter physics and quantum information, but the paper is primarily a review of condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models describing internal conversion, including nonradiative mechanisms and their incorporation into application-oriented studies.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical approaches and an outlook on their integration into practical applications.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature but need better integration with applied fields like photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored. This review aims to bridge the gap between classical skyrmion physics and quantum mechanics.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum tunneling, and quantum-classical correspondence, synthesizing results from condensed matter physics.
result: It highlights that skyrmions can exhibit quantum effects such as tunneling and superposition, and discusses how these could be harnessed for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions offer a new platform for studying topological quantum phenomena and may enable novel quantum technologies, but the field is still nascent.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy, and to probe discrete fundamental symmetries, by searching for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model.
method: The paper reviews a wide range of theoretical models and experimental techniques used to search for spin-dependent exotic interactions, including precision measurements with atomic, molecular, and optical systems.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic boson-mediated interactions and highlights the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, and ongoing and future experiments will further constrain or potentially detect these interactions.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions in stars occur at very low energies with small rates, making direct laboratory measurements difficult. Understanding these reactions is crucial for stellar evolution and element formation.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical methods and experimental challenges in low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand stellar nuclear reactions, which are governed by quantum phenomena at low energies.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but some measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to novel materials.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and phenomena where bounds are exceeded, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions behind the bounds, and shows how to design materials that exploit these violations.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplied assumptions; this insight can guide development of materials with extreme properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in various platforms.
result: Summarizes current progress and challenges in simulating exotic geometries with ultracold atoms, photonics, and electronic systems.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with potential to bridge condensed matter, quantum information, and high-energy physics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence, collapse, and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and massive quantum systems may serve as probes to test quantum aspects of gravity.
method: The paper reviews existing theories and experimental approaches, including matter-wave interferometry and proposals for gravity-mediated entanglement tests.
result: It summarizes the current state of the art and outlines ongoing experiments that could reveal whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
conclusion: The results of these experiments will guide the theoretical description of gravity on laboratory scales, but no new results are presented.

title: Emergent Trion Resonance Driven By Lattice Reconstruction In A Moiré Superlattice
authors: Zhida Liu, Haonan Wang, Xiaohui Liu, Yue Ni, Hongtao Yan, Frank Y. Gao, Saba Arash, Hyunsue Kim, Dong Seob Kim, Xiangcheng Liu, Xiaoxiao Yu, Yongxin Zeng, Jiamin Quan, Di Huang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Edoardo Baldini, Keji Lai, Allan H. Macdonald, Chih-Kang Shih, Jamie Warner, Li Yang, And Xiaoqin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zhida Liu, Haonan Wang, Xiaohui Liu, Yue Ni, Hongtao Yan, Frank Y. Gao, Saba Arash, Hyunsue Kim, Dong Seob Kim, Xiangcheng Liu, Xiaoxiao Yu, Yongxin Zeng, Jiamin Quan, Di Huang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Edoardo Baldini, Keji Lai, Allan H. MacDonald, Chih-Kang Shih, Jamie Warner, Li Yang, and Xiaoqin Li

We investigate how many-electron excited states emerge in twisted [MATH] homobilayers when the lattice reconstructions evolve. Notably, we identify a new trion resonance that arises in the transition regime of lattice reconstruction, where gradual changes in atomic alignment between t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036902] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies emergent trion resonances in twisted MoSe2 homobilayers driven by lattice reconstruction, a topic in condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how many-electron excited states emerge in moiré superlattices as lattice reconstruction evolves.
method: Optical spectroscopy and theoretical modeling of twisted MoSe2 homobilayers with varying twist angles.
result: A new trion resonance is identified in the transition regime of lattice reconstruction, linked to changes in atomic alignment.
conclusion: Lattice reconstruction plays a key role in determining the optical properties of moiré superlattices, revealing new correlated phases.

title: Probing Dielectric Screening In Van Der Waals Heterostructures Via Pressure-Tuned Exciton Rydberg Series
authors: Shalini Badola, Adlen Smiri, Thomas Pelini, Aditi Moghe, Tristan Riccardi, Amit Pawbake, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Iann C. Gerber, And Clément Faugeras
abstract:
Author(s): Shalini Badola, Adlen Smiri, Thomas Pelini, Aditi Moghe, Tristan Riccardi, Amit Pawbake, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Iann C. Gerber, and Clément Faugeras

Excitons in two-dimensional semiconductors are directly exposed to the environment and are sensitive to the dielectric properties of their surrounding. Here, we show that the Rydberg series of excited states of excitons in a monolayer [MATH] encapsulated in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 036903] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton Rydberg series in monolayer WSe2 under pressure to probe dielectric screening in van der Waals heterostructures.
motivation: Understanding dielectric screening in 2D semiconductors is important for optoelectronic applications, but the paper focuses on exciton physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors perform photoluminescence spectroscopy on monolayer WSe2 encapsulated in hBN under hydrostatic pressure, measuring the energies of exciton Rydberg states.
result: They observe a pressure-induced redshift of the exciton ground state and changes in the Rydberg series, which they attribute to modifications in dielectric screening.
conclusion: The work provides insights into dielectric screening in van der Waals heterostructures but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optical Soliton Cooper Pairs In Mamyshev Oscillators
authors: Chenxiao Hao, Tianhao Xian, Zhenghu Chang, Yahan Du, And Li Zhan
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxiao Hao, Tianhao Xian, Zhenghu Chang, Yahan Du, and Li Zhan

The framework of superconductivity unveiled the striking concept that electrons form Cooper pairs through the subtle interplay of lattice vibrations, surmounting their Coulombic repulsion in the process. The concept of Cooper pairs has been established beyond the Fermi system, and this pairing mecha…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033801] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an optical analog of Cooper pairs using soliton interactions in Mamyshev oscillators.
motivation: To explore whether the Cooper pairing mechanism from superconductivity can be realized in optical systems, potentially enabling new forms of light-matter interactions.
method: The authors theoretically model and simulate soliton dynamics in a Mamyshev oscillator, demonstrating that two solitons can form a bound state analogous to Cooper pairs via a nonlinear interaction mediated by the oscillator's gain and filtering.
result: They show that under specific conditions, solitons can pair up with a binding energy that depends on system parameters, resembling the behavior of Cooper pairs in superconductors.
conclusion: The work provides a classical optical analogue of Cooper pairing, which may inspire new approaches to robust light states but does not directly contribute to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Atomic Clock Frequency Ratios With Fractional Uncertainty $≤3.2×{10}^{−18}$
authors: Alexander Aeppli et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Aeppli et al. (BACON Collaboration)

We report high-precision frequency ratio measurements between optical atomic clocks based on [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. With total fractional uncertainties at or below [MATH], these measurements meet an important milestone criterion for redefinit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 033201] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: High-precision frequency ratio measurements between optical atomic clocks with fractional uncertainty at or below 3.2×10^{-18}.
motivation: To meet a milestone criterion for redefinition of the second based on optical clocks.
method: Frequency ratio measurements using optical atomic clocks based on different atomic species.
result: Achieved total fractional uncertainties at or below 3.2×10^{-18}.
conclusion: These measurements support the potential redefinition of the second.

title: Optical Repumping And Controlled Population Transfer In A Two-color Magneto-optical Trap
authors: Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, And Philippe Wilhelm Courteille
abstract:
Author(s): Shubha Deutschle, Lőrinc Sárkány, Milán János Negyedi, József Fortágh, Andreas Günther, and Philippe Wilhelm Courteille

We study a repumping transition for [MATH] atoms trapped in a blue magneto-optical trap. We show that, while the repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than for traditional schemes, it is sufficient for recycling all atoms, provided the repumping laser beams are …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013715] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an optical repumping scheme for atoms in a two-color magneto-optical trap, focusing on experimental efficiency and population transfer.
motivation: To improve repumping efficiency in magneto-optical traps for better atom trapping and cooling.
method: Experimental study of a repumping transition using two-color laser beams and measurement of fluorescence and atom number.
result: The repumping efficiency is about three orders of magnitude smaller than traditional schemes but sufficient for recycling all atoms.
conclusion: The proposed repumping scheme is viable for atom trapping despite lower efficiency, offering an alternative for specific experimental setups.

title: Interelectronic Correlation: Neutral And Ionized Atoms In Conjugate Spaces
authors: M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, And J. C. Angulo
abstract:
Author(s): M. M. Gutiérrez-Vílchez, I. López-García, and J. C. Angulo

The intercorrelation level among constituent electrons of a multielectronic system is quantified by comparing the electron-pair density and the product of its marginal one-particle densities. The resulting comparison is interpreted as a measure of the interelectronic correlation and/or mutual inform…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012812] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies interelectronic correlation in multielectronic systems using electron-pair densities and mutual information.
motivation: To develop a measure of interelectronic correlation that can be applied to both neutral and ionized atoms.
method: The authors compare the electron-pair density with the product of marginal one-particle densities, interpreting the difference as a measure of correlation.
result: They provide a quantification of interelectronic correlation in conjugate spaces (position and momentum).
conclusion: The proposed measure effectively captures interelectronic correlation and can be used for various atomic systems.

title: Parametric Mössbauer Radiation In The Grazing-diffraction Geometry: Specular Diffraction And Superradiant Amplification
authors: Ze-An Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, And Jörg Evers
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-an Peng, Christoph H. Keitel, and Jörg Evers

Parametric x-ray radiation (PXR) is a tunable and versatile x-ray production mechanism that relies on relativistic electrons traversing through a crystal. When the crystal contains Mössbauer nuclei, they may also contribute to the x-ray generation, giving rise to spectrally narrow parametric Mössbau…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013115] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies parametric Mössbauer radiation in grazing-diffraction geometry, focusing on specular diffraction and superradiant amplification.
motivation: To explore a new x-ray production mechanism that combines parametric x-ray radiation with Mössbauer nuclei for spectrally narrow emission.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the grazing-diffraction geometry for parametric Mössbauer radiation, deriving expressions for the radiation field and considering superradiant amplification.
result: They find that specular diffraction can enhance the radiation and that superradiant amplification occurs under certain conditions.
conclusion: The proposed geometry offers a way to generate narrow-band x-ray radiation with potential applications in nuclear quantum optics.

title: Revealing Hidden Topology Of Complex Vector Beams Via Plasmonic Interactions
authors: Sahil Sahoo, Ahmed Lafeef Ettapuram Naduvilepurayil, Andre Yaroshevsky, Peter Banzer, And Yuri Gorodetski
abstract:
Author(s): Sahil Sahoo, Ahmed Lafeef Ettapuram Naduvilepurayil, Andre Yaroshevsky, Peter Banzer, and Yuri Gorodetski

Structured light beams with space-variant polarization can be efficiently generated using a voltage-tunable nematic liquid crystal ([MATH] plate). By appropriately selecting the input state and the retardation of the [MATH] plate, an optical field acquires a spatially structured polarization distribution …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013514] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to reveal hidden polarization topologies in complex vector beams using plasmonic interactions.
motivation: Complex vector beams with space-variant polarization can carry topological features that are not directly observable; the authors aim to uncover these hidden topologies.
method: They use a voltage-tunable liquid crystal q-plate to generate structured light and probe it via plasmonic interactions, analyzing the resulting near-field patterns.
result: The plasmonic interaction maps the polarization topology onto the near-field intensity, allowing reconstruction of the beam's topological charge and polarization distribution.
conclusion: Plasmonic interactions provide a practical tool for characterizing complex vector beams, with potential applications in optical manipulation and imaging.

title: Coexisting Paramagnetic Spins And Long-range Magnetic Order In ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{4}{({\mathrm{Ru}}_{0.92}{\mathrm{Ir}}_{0.08})}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10}$
authors: Farhan Islam, Jiasen Guo, Wei Tian, Bing Li, Xudong Huai, Thao T. Tran, Gang Cao, Zachary Morgan, And Feng Ye
abstract:
Author(s): Farhan Islam, Jiasen Guo, Wei Tian, Bing Li, Xudong Huai, Thao T. Tran, Gang Cao, Zachary Morgan, and Feng Ye

We investigate the effect of dilute Ir substitution on the magnetism of the trimer-based ruthenate [MATH] using neutron diffraction, magnetic susceptibility measurements, first-principles calculations, and atomistic simulations. Neutron diffraction show…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034416] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of a ruthenate material with dilute iridium substitution using neutron diffraction and other techniques.
motivation: To understand how dilute Ir substitution affects the magnetism of trimer-based ruthenate Ba4(Ru1-xIrx)3O10, particularly the coexistence of paramagnetic spins and long-range order.
method: Neutron diffraction, magnetic susceptibility measurements, first-principles calculations, and atomistic simulations.
result: Dilute Ir substitution induces coexisting paramagnetic spins and long-range magnetic order, modifying the magnetic structure.
conclusion: The study reveals complex magnetic behavior in doped ruthenates, relevant to condensed matter physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Cubic-in-magnetization Contributions To The Magneto-optic Kerr Effect Investigated For Ni(001) And Ni(111) Thin Films
authors: Robin Silber, Maik Gaerner, Kamil Postava, Jaroslav Hamrle, And Timo Kuschel
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Silber, Maik Gaerner, Kamil Postava, Jaroslav Hamrle, and Timo Kuschel

The existence of higher-order effects in magnetization in magneto-transport and magneto-optic phenomena is well known. These effects are of importance not only in research but also directly in applications. Anisotropic magneto-resistance, anisotropic magneto-thermopower, quadratic magneto-optic Kerr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014418] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates higher-order magneto-optic Kerr effects in nickel thin films, focusing on cubic-in-magnetization contributions.
motivation: Higher-order magneto-optic effects are important for both fundamental research and applications, but their detailed characterization in nickel films is lacking.
method: The authors measure the magneto-optic Kerr effect for Ni(001) and Ni(111) thin films and analyze the cubic-in-magnetization contributions using symmetry arguments and experimental data.
result: They identify and quantify the cubic-in-magnetization contributions to the Kerr effect, showing distinct behaviors for different crystallographic orientations.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed understanding of higher-order magneto-optic effects in nickel, which may be relevant for magnetic sensing and spintronics applications.

title: Origin Of Acceptor Preference In Silicon, Diamond, And Silicon Carbide
authors: Xuefen Cai, Feiyang Chen, Huachun Wang, Yi-Feng Zheng, Bin Wang, And Su-Huai Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Xuefen Cai, Feiyang Chen, Huachun Wang, Yi-Feng Zheng, Bin Wang, and Su-Huai Wei

Silicon, diamond, and their compound silicon carbide play pivotal roles in electronic science and technology. Trivalent impurities such as B and Al are the typical choices for [MATH]-type doping in these semiconductors. Intriguingly, B dominates in Si and diamond, while Al is preferred in SiC for indus…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045203] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the origin of acceptor preference (B vs Al) in silicon, diamond, and silicon carbide semiconductors using first-principles calculations.
motivation: Understanding why B is preferred in Si and diamond while Al is preferred in SiC is important for optimizing p-type doping in these technologically crucial semiconductors.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) are performed to analyze the electronic structure and formation energies of B and Al acceptors in Si, diamond, and SiC.
result: The preference is explained by differences in atomic size, electronegativity, and the resulting lattice relaxation and electronic effects.
conclusion: The study provides a unified explanation for acceptor preference across these materials, aiding in the design of better p-type dopants.

title: Computer Simulations Of The Stark Effect In The Helium-$β$ Complex Of Krypton In Inertial Confinement Fusion Conditions
authors: G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, And M. A. Gigosos
abstract:
Author(s): G. Pérez-Callejo, E. Stambulchik, R. Florido, and M. A. Gigosos

There is an ongoing interest in using spectroscopy in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments, where dopants such as krypton can provide vital information about the temperature and density of the imploding plasma. While the most advanced tools for calculating Stark profiles are computer simula…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015212] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses computer simulations to study the Stark effect in krypton under inertial confinement fusion conditions, focusing on plasma spectroscopy.
motivation: To improve diagnostic capabilities in inertial confinement fusion experiments by modeling spectral line shapes of dopant krypton.
method: Computer simulations of Stark-broadened line profiles for the helium-beta complex of krypton in dense plasmas.
result: Simulated Stark profiles that can be used to infer plasma temperature and density from spectroscopic data.
conclusion: The simulations provide a tool for interpreting ICF spectra, but the work is applied plasma physics with no quantum information or thermodynamics contribution.

title: Dynamical Origin Of Extreme Events In Mutually Coupled And Networked Brusselator
authors: S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, And I. Manimehan
abstract:
Author(s): S. V. Manivelan, S. Sabarathinam, K. Thamilmaran, and I. Manimehan

This study investigates the dynamical origins and statistical properties of extreme events (EEs) in a diffusively coupled theoretical Brusselator system, extending from pairwise interactions to globally coupled networks. Statistically, the emergence of EEs is characterized by heavy-tailed probabilit…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014217] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies extreme events in a diffusively coupled Brusselator system, a chemical reaction model, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamical origin of extreme events in nonlinear systems is important for predicting rare but impactful phenomena.
method: The authors analyze a diffusively coupled Brusselator model, from pairwise to globally coupled networks, using statistical and dynamical systems methods.
result: Extreme events are characterized by heavy-tailed probability distributions and are linked to specific dynamical instabilities.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the emergence of extreme events in coupled nonlinear oscillators, but does not involve quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Unified Ott-Antonsen Framework For Stability And Bifurcations In Ring Swarmalators
authors: Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, And Xingang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Xu, Wenhan Xu, and Xingang Wang

Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014212] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework for analyzing stability and bifurcations in ring swarmalator systems, which combine phase oscillations with spatial swarming.
motivation: Swarmalators exhibit rich collective dynamics, but a general theoretical framework for their stability and bifurcations was lacking.
method: The authors extend the Ott-Antonsen ansatz to ring swarmalator models, deriving reduced equations for the order parameters and analyzing their stability and bifurcations.
result: They obtain analytical conditions for synchronization, clustering, and wave states, and validate them with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The unified framework provides a powerful tool for understanding collective behavior in active matter systems with both phase and spatial degrees of freedom.

title: Filtered Rayleigh-Ritz And The Prony-Ritz Equivalence Class
authors: Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, And Michael L. Wagman
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Abbott, Daniel C. Hackett, George T. Fleming, Dimitra A. Pefkou, and Michael L. Wagman

Recent work [ 112, 054506 (2025);
tldr: This paper presents a method for extracting energy spectra from correlation functions in lattice quantum field theory using a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz approach and establishes an equivalence class with Prony-type methods.
motivation: Extracting excited-state energies and matrix elements from Euclidean correlation functions is a fundamental challenge in lattice QCD, and existing methods like the Lanczos algorithm have limitations.
method: The authors develop a filtered Rayleigh-Ritz method that uses a filtering function to isolate eigenstates, and show that it is equivalent to a class of Prony-like methods, providing a unified framework.
result: The method yields accurate energy levels and matrix elements for test systems, and the equivalence class clarifies the relationship between different extraction techniques.
conclusion: The filtered Rayleigh-Ritz approach offers a robust and systematic way to extract spectral information from correlation functions, with connections to other methods that enhance its utility.

title: Inhibition Of Explosive Transitions In Spreading Dynamics By Nonlinear Higher-order Adaptation
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Zhihao Han, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

The coevolution of structure and dynamics, known as adaptation, is a fundamental property in various systems and drives diverse emergent behaviors. However, the adaptation in most works primarily stems from pairwise situations, which is insufficient to capture ubiquitous higher-order characteristics…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033068] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how nonlinear higher-order adaptation can inhibit explosive transitions in spreading dynamics on complex networks.
motivation: Explosive transitions in spreading dynamics are undesirable in many real systems, and understanding how adaptation mechanisms can prevent them is important for controlling epidemics or information spread.
method: The authors develop a model of spreading dynamics with higher-order (non-pairwise) adaptation rules and analyze it using mean-field theory and numerical simulations on synthetic and real networks.
result: They find that nonlinear higher-order adaptation can effectively suppress explosive transitions, leading to continuous phase transitions instead.
conclusion: Higher-order adaptation mechanisms provide a robust way to control explosive spreading phenomena, offering insights for designing resilient networks.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy, using time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in van der Waals heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling the microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) to probe the dynamics of charge transfer in a heterostructure under different excitation energies.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways for charge transfer that depend on the excitation energy, revealing a competition between direct and indirect transfer mechanisms.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into how excitation energy can be used to control charge transfer pathways, which may help optimize device performance.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism underlying abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical framework for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for training dynamics.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in two-dimensional photonic crystals with stealthy hyperuniform disorder, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of radiative loss in disordered photonic materials, impacting their design for optical applications.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review three real-space techniques that provide direct access to such information.

method: Neutron inelastic scattering experiments on liquid hydrogen sulfide to measure its dynamic structure factor and identify collective modes.
result: Fast sound is preserved in hydrogen sulfide, but the secondary weakly dispersive mode characteristic of hydrogen-bonded liquids is absent.
conclusion: The absence of the secondary mode confirms its association with hydrogen-bond networks, highlighting the unique dynamics of hydrogen-bonded liquids.

title: Cholesteric Fingers From A Magnetic Perspective: Topology, Energetics, And Interactions
authors: Takayuki Shigenaga And Andrey O. Leonov
abstract:
Author(s): Takayuki Shigenaga and Andrey O. Leonov

Chiral liquid crystals and chiral magnets host a wide variety of topological solitons governed by closely related continuum theories, namely the Frank-Oseen model for liquid crystals and the Dzyaloshinskii model for chiral magnets. Here we exploit this correspondence to develop a unified theoretical…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015411] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological solitons in chiral liquid crystals and magnets, developing a unified theoretical framework.
motivation: To exploit the correspondence between chiral liquid crystals and chiral magnets for a unified description of topological solitons.
method: The authors use continuum theories (Frank-Oseen and Dzyaloshinskii models) to analyze cholesteric fingers from a magnetic perspective.
result: A unified theoretical framework is developed, revealing common topological and energetic properties.
conclusion: The correspondence between the two systems can be leveraged for cross-disciplinary insights.

title: Multiphoton Ionization With Three-dimensional Light Fields
authors: D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, And M. Wollenhaupt
abstract:
Author(s): D. Köhnke, H.-C. Ahlswede, T. Bayer, and M. Wollenhaupt

We employ, for the first time, bichromatic three-dimensional (3D) polarization-shaped ultrashort laser fields in atomic multiphoton ionization to create previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets. The 3D fields are created by the noncollinear superposition of two polarizatio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033048] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses bichromatic three-dimensional polarization-shaped laser fields to create free-electron angular momentum wave packets in atomic multiphoton ionization.
motivation: To generate previously inaccessible free-electron angular momentum wave packets using tailored light fields.
method: Noncollinear superposition of two polarization-shaped ultrashort laser pulses to create 3D fields, applied to atomic multiphoton ionization.
result: Demonstration of controlled electron wave packet creation via 3D light fields.
conclusion: The technique enables new control over electron dynamics in strong-field ionization.

title: Anomalous Pressure Dependence Of The Bulk Modulus And Yb Valence In Cubic YbPd
authors: B. Tegomo Chiogo, V. Balédent, J.-P. Rueff, E. Saïman, V. Poree, T. Schweitzer, D. Wong, C. Schulz, T. Mazet, A. Chainani, D. Malterre, And K. Habicht

We investigate the Yb valence instabilities in the strongly correlated YbPd compound using resonant x-ray emission spectroscopy as a function of pressure across the charge-order (CO) transition. At a low temperature ([MATH]) in the CO phase, the Yb [MATH] valence …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033055] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the pressure dependence of Yb valence and bulk modulus in cubic YbPd, focusing on charge-order transition and strongly correlated electron behavior.
motivation: To understand the anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk modulus in YbPd and its relation to Yb valence instabilities across the charge-order transition.
method: Resonant x-ray emission spectroscopy and bulk modulus measurements under varying pressure and temperature.
result: Observed anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk modulus correlated with changes in Yb valence across the charge-order transition.
conclusion: The anomalous behavior is linked to valence fluctuations and charge ordering in strongly correlated YbPd.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film

Hwang, And Zhi-Xun Shen

Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films under compressive strain and doping.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The electronic structure of bilayer nickelates is sensitive to strain and doping, but the out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions.
motivation: To explore whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic protocols.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail in finding collisions, suggesting potential cryptographic applications.
conclusion: Simple neural networks may exhibit collision resistance, relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine learning.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
